events.headline: Stock market rattled by oil supply chain disruptions
events.summary: Senewiratne A Brent crude oil price increase due to supply chain disruptions in the Middle East owing to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabian targets, negatively impacted the CSE yesterday. Most foreign and local investors were worried over a probable oil price hike in Sri Lanka that would impact the manufacturing and production sectors in the country. The All Share Price Index went down by 11.06 points, while the S and P SL20 went up by 0.56 points. Turnover stood at Rs 656 million with two crossings. Those crossings were: Access Engineering 1 million shares crossed to the tune of Rs 74.5 million and its shares traded at Rs 74.50 and Commercial Bank 303,000 shares crossed for Rs 59 million; its shares traded at Rs 195.

sources.headline: Stock market rattled by oil supply chain disruptions

events.headline: CRIB expands credit information ecosystem
events.summary: Jayasinghe, Dumbara Micro Credit CEO Gnanasiri Abeywardena and Sejaya Micro Credit CEO Rizanth Francis Chief Guest CRIB Chairman and Central Bank Deputy Governor K.G.P. Sirikumara - Onboards four licenced microfinance institutions The Credit Information Bureau of Sri Lanka (CRIB) has announced a significant expansion of the country’s credit information ecosystem with the onboarding of four licenced microfinance institutions, following the publication of the relevant Government Gazette Notification. This initiative marks an important step towards strengthening credit information sharing within the microfinance sector, enhancing the availability of reliable credit information, and promoting greater financial inclusion by facilitating improved access to formal credit for underserved individuals and businesses.

events.headline: CBSL stresses public trust in AI adoption
events.summary: Sri Lanka (CBSL) has stressed that public trust must remain central to the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as the technology increasingly influences institutional decision-making, CBSL Governor Dr P Nandalal Weerasinghe said at its 76th Anniversary Oration on Friday (23). Speaking at the event, held under the theme The Intelligent Central Bank: Building Trust in the Age of AI , Dr Weerasinghe said: “As we embrace emerging technologies, we must ensure that innovation strengthens rather than diminishes trust. AI is rapidly transforming the way institutions generate insights, make decisions, deliver services, and manage risk.” “The Central Bank’s trust has always been our most valuable asset.

sources.headline: CBSL stresses public trust in AI adoption

events.headline: Returns on ethics: A new compass for global finance in an age of debt and inequality
events.summary: MSc (NTU), MBA (Sri J) As the world moves closer to the 2030 deadline for achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), a troubling reality is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. Global wealth continues to expand, financial markets reach record valuations, and technological innovation accelerates at an unprecedented pace. Yet millions of people are falling behind, public services are under strain, and environmental degradation continues unabated. The question confronting policymakers is no longer whether the global economic model is under stress, but whether the metrics guiding that model remain fit for purpose. For decades, economic success has been measured through indicators such as Gross Domestic Product (GDP), shareholder returns and Return on Equity (RoE).

sources.headline: Returns on ethics: A new compass for global finance in an age of debt and inequality

events.headline: CSE starts week in red, down 0.23%
events.summary: The Colombo stock market yesterday opened the week in red, extending losses into a sixth consecutive session. events.headline: CBSL marks 76th Anniversary with oration on AI and Public Trust
events.summary: The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) marked its 76th anniversary with a high-level oration on how artificial intelligence is reshaping central banking, held at the Central Bank Atrium on 23 October 2026. The oration was delivered by Shirin Hamid, Chief Information Officer and Director of the Information Technology Department at the International Monetary Fund (IMF). Her address, titled “The Intelligent Central Bank: Building Trust in the Age of AI,” explored both the promise and the pitfalls of deploying AI in monetary and financial institutions. Hamid said AI holds significant potential to strengthen how central banks carry out their mandates, but warned that the associated risks demand careful management.

sources.headline: CBSL marks 76th Anniversary with oration on AI and Public Trust

events.headline: International Monetary Fund sees Sri Lanka primed for AI leapfrog
events.summary: Shirin Hamid By Shabiya Ali Ahlam Sri Lanka has won praise from the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) technology chief for building the digital foundations to leapfrog into the artificial intelligence (AI) era, with a call to match the technological ambition with investment in people, sound judgment and accountability. I think you are closer to this future than you think,” visiting IMF Chief Information Officer Shirin Hamid told the Central Bank of Sri Lanka’s (CBSL) 76th anniversary oration. Speaking on ‘The Intelligent Central Bank: Building Trust in the Age of AI’, Hamid highlighted Sri Lanka’s expanding digital payments, digital identity preparations and plans for secure data sharing as foundations for the next stage of transformation.

sources.headline: International Monetary Fund sees Sri Lanka primed for AI leapfrog

events.headline: Minister highlights new investment opportunities ahead of SL EXPO 2027
events.summary: Sri Lanka made a direct pitch to British investors at a special Business and Investment Forum in London, presenting the island as a stable, reform-driven economy ready for deeper partnership with the United Kingdom. Held under the patronage of Trade Minister Wasantha Samarasinghe, the forum drew business leaders, investors and industry representatives from both countries. Sri Lanka’s delegation included High Commissioner Nimal Senadheera, UK Trade Envoy Lord Hannett, Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development Secretary Thilaka Jayasundara, EDB Chairman/CEO Mangala Wijesinghe and Board of Investment (BOI) representatives. Strong participation from British firms in IT, real estate, energy and food processing, the Minister said, “Clearly reflects their keen interest in expanding trade and investment cooperation with Sri Lanka,” He noted that the UK is among Sri Lanka’s most important trading partners and its third-largest export market.

sources.headline: Minister highlights new investment opportunities ahead of SL EXPO 2027

events.headline: Policy priorities to achieve durable growth in Sri Lanka
events.summary: S ustaining Sri Lanka’s post-crisis macroeconomic stability requires productivity-enhancing reforms to achieve durable and inclusive growth. Against this backdrop, the Institute of Policy Studies of Sri Lanka (IPS) hosted a roundtable discussion on 14 October 2026 on its flagship publication, Sri Lanka State of the Economy 2026, to discuss policy priorities to rebuild the country’s economic foundations amidst ongoing domestic and global uncertainties. IPS Research Fellows Dr Asanka Wijesinghe and Dr Lakmini Fernando presented key findings, followed by interventions from Dr Yashodha Senadheera, Deputy Director of the Economic Research Department of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL); Dr Liliya Aleksanyan, Senior Country Economist for Sri Lanka at the Asian Development Bank (ADB); Mr. Sanjaya Ariyawansa, Senior Economist at Sampath Bank; and other invited parties.

sources.headline: Policy priorities to achieve durable growth in Sri Lanka
Beyond recovery: Policy priorities to achieve durable growth in Sri Lanka

events.headline: Placating demons still
events.summary: Sri Lanka has spent recent weeks listening to a curse. Vas Kavi, anonymous verses invoking malevolent forces against the country’s rulers, have spread rapidly across social media. The latest calls on Vajrapani, a fearsome form of the deity Sakra, to strike down an unnamed ruler accused of gaining power through falsehoods. The verses followed a campaign by a group of Buddhist monks demanding the release of a fellow monk sentenced to six years’ rigorous imprisonment for contempt of court. During the protest, participants reportedly drove wooden nails into a clay effigy in the name of the demon Maha Sona.

sources.headline: Placating demons still

events.headline: Renewable Energy: Financing channels, infrastructure not kept pace
events.summary: Sri Lanka has made progress on realising transition towards renewable energy, transmission capacity, market design, financing channels and digital infrastructure have not kept pace with the ongoing renewable energy (RE) capacity additions; necessitating an integrated system to absorb RE additions, Institute of Policy Studies (IPS) Research Fellow Dr Erandathie Pathiraja said. Presenting a chapter in the IPS State of the Economy report titled; ‘Renewable Energy Transition: A Strategic Imperative for Energy Security, Economic Resilience and Durable Growth’, Dr Pathiraja compared the distributed generation of solar panels with the centralised model: “In centralised systems the power plant and transmissions lines are built, but when it comes to renewable energy generation, the renewable sources are scattered.” “For example when you take roof top solar producers, the system should be capable of absorbing that.

sources.headline: Renewable Energy: Financing channels, infrastructure not kept pace

events.headline: ‘Tertiary education advancement, key to producing workers with problem-solving skills’
events.summary: Senewiratne Tertiary education is vital for sustainable growth and for producing skilled workers with critical thinking, problem-solving and advanced tech skills, central to boosting productivity , competitiveness and innovation in the economy, said Dr. Nisha Arunatilake- Director of Research, Institute of Policy Studies (IPS). ‘STEM fields including science, technology, engineering and maths are key to fostering ongoing innovation- led growth, expanding economic activity and creating jobs for graduates and supporting industries, Dr Arunatilake said at a round table discussion held recently at the IPS auditorium in Colombo under the topic ‘Durable Growth in Sri Lanka: Advancing Human Capital for Inclusive Prosperity’.

audit.headline: Building through challenges: Why construction matters to Sri Lanka’s economic future
audit.summary: Sri Lanka’s construction and property development industry has travelled through one of the most difficult periods in its history. Developers, contractors, engineers, suppliers and financial institutions have had to navigate economic instability, escalating construction costs, high financing expenses, exchange-rate fluctuations, taxation changes, shortages of skilled labour and disruptions to material supplies. For an industry in which projects are conceived, financed and delivered over several years, these are not temporary inconveniences. They can fundamentally change the economics of developments that were planned and priced under completely different market conditions. Nevertheless, I remain confident about the long-term future of Sri Lanka’s construction sector. Construction should not be viewed merely as an industry that builds apartments, offices or infrastructure.
audit.body: Sri Lanka’s construction and property development industry has travelled through one of the most difficult periods in its history. Developers, contractors, engineers, suppliers and financial institutions have had to navigate economic instability, escalating construction costs, high financing expenses, exchange-rate fluctuations, taxation changes, shortages of skilled labour and disruptions to material supplies. For an industry in which projects are conceived, financed and delivered over several years, these are not temporary inconveniences. They can fundamentally change the economics of developments that were planned and priced under completely different market conditions. Nevertheless, I remain confident about the long-term future of Sri Lanka’s construction sector. Construction should not be viewed merely as an industry that builds apartments, offices or infrastructure. It is an economic ecosystem that creates employment, supports numerous industries, attracts investment and produces long-term national assets. The challenge now is to transform the resilience demonstrated by the industry into sustainable growth. Time has become a cost Property development requires substantial investment long before revenue is fully realised. Land must be acquired, designs prepared, approvals obtained, financing arranged, contractors mobilised and construction completed before the final value of a project can be realised. During this period, economic conditions can change considerably. A project planned when interest rates, exchange rates, material prices and taxation were at one level may ultimately have to be completed under entirely different conditions. Once commitments have been made to customers, however, responsible developers must continue working towards completion. This is why time has become one of the most expensive components of construction. Every unnecessary month lost through approval delays, financing issues, procurement difficulties or inefficient project management adds cost. Interest continues to accumulate, site overheads remain, contractors stay mobilised and customers wait longer. Improving the speed of project delivery is therefore not merely a matter of convenience. It has a direct impact on affordability and investment. Affordability must remain central The industry’s next major challenge is maintaining affordability. When cement, steel, aluminium, lifts, air-conditioning systems, electrical equipment, sanitaryware and labour become more expensive, the obvious response may appear to be increasing selling prices. But developers cannot indefinitely transfer every cost increase to customers. Household incomes and purchasing power do not automatically increase whenever construction costs rise. The sustainable solution must therefore come from productivity. Better architectural planning, value engineering, stronger procurement, reduced material wastage, modern construction methods and improved project management can collectively reduce unnecessary development costs. Technology will also play an increasingly important role. Building Information Modelling, digital project monitoring, AI-assisted planning, modern formwork and other construction technologies can improve productivity and shorten development periods. The objective must be to maintain the right balance between quality, affordability, commercial viability and long-term value. Financing and development must work together Construction is highly capital-intensive, making the banking sector an essential participant in the development process. Banks understandably have a responsibility to protect depositors and manage credit risk. Developers have an equally important obligation to demonstrate financial discipline, transparency and the ability to complete projects. However, large property developments can extend over several years. Financing structures should therefore recognise realistic construction programmes and project cash flows. Excessive financing costs ultimately become part of the cost of development. If projects are delayed, these costs compound further. Closer cooperation between financially responsible developers and financial institutions can create better outcomes for both the industry and customers. Developers must reciprocate by strengthening collections, controlling expenditure, managing cash flow carefully and giving priority to completing projects already undertaken. Faster approvals without lowering standards Regulatory efficiency is another area where Sri Lanka can make significant progress. Planning controls, environmental requirements, fire and safety standards, traffic considerations and infrastructure coordination are essential for responsible development. The issue is not whether Sri Lanka needs regulation. It unquestionably does. The question is whether those regulations can be administered more efficiently and predictably. When approvals take unnecessarily long periods, capital remains idle while financing and other costs continue accumulating. Sri Lanka should progressively move towards an integrated digital approval framework with transparent requirements, clearly defined responsibilities and measurable processing timelines. Faster approvals should never mean weaker standards. Sri Lanka needs strong standards delivered efficiently. This is particularly important when competing internationally for investment. Investors can accommodate demanding regulations when the requirements are clear and consistently applied. What discourages investment is uncertainty. Protecting our human capital Sri Lanka has produced highly capable engineers, architects, quantity surveyors, project managers, technical officers and skilled construction workers. However, migration has created shortages across several professional and technical categories. The response should be greater investment in people. Construction companies must provide opportunities for young professionals, apprentices and trainees to acquire practical experience while ensuring that knowledge held by senior professionals is transferred to the next generation. Technology should support rather than undermine this process. Its greatest value is not simply replacing manpower but enabling people to become significantly more productive. Sri Lanka’s skilled human capital remains one of our strongest competitive advantages. Construction’s wider economic contribution The economic impact of construction extends far beyond a building site. A major development generates work for architects, engineers, quantity surveyors, banks, insurance companies, lawyers, accountants, material manufacturers, transport operators, equipment suppliers and numerous subcontractors. Thousands of skilled and unskilled workers depend directly or indirectly on construction activity. After a building is completed, economic activity continues through facility management, security, maintenance, utilities and other services. Construction therefore has a powerful multiplier effect. When construction slows substantially, the consequences spread throughout the economy. When responsible construction expands, the benefits similarly extend across businesses and households. For this reason, a healthy construction sector should form part of Sri Lanka’s broader economic growth strategy. The Diaspora opportunity Sri Lanka also has considerable potential to attract greater property investment from Sri Lankans living overseas. Our diaspora across the United Kingdom, Europe, Australia, Canada, the Middle East, the United States and elsewhere maintains strong personal and economic connections with the country. Many want to own a home in Sri Lanka, provide accommodation for family members or maintain a long-term investment here. This represents an important opportunity to attract foreign-currency investment. But overseas buyers expect international standards. They require transparency, professional communication, construction quality, dependable completion schedules and confidence in the legal and regulatory environment. The more we strengthen these areas, the more competitive Sri Lanka becomes as an international property investment destination. Developers must accept responsibility too It would be incorrect to discuss the industry’s challenges while placing responsibility entirely on government, banks or economic circumstances. The private sector must also raise its standards. Developers must strengthen corporate governance, financial discipline, transparency, construction quality and customer communication. Most importantly, the industry must recognise a fundamental principle: Launching a project is not the real achievement. Completing it successfully and handing it over to customers is the true measure of a developer. Customer confidence is one of the industry’s most valuable assets. It can take years to establish and very little time to damage. Developers must therefore honour commitments, communicate transparently, manage capital responsibly and prioritise the completion of projects already undertaken. Building a Stronger Sri Lanka Sri Lanka’s construction industry has demonstrated remarkable resilience through an exceptionally difficult economic period. The responsibility now is to convert that resilience into sustainable growth. Government, regulators, banks, developers, contractors and professional institutions all have a role. We need stable policies, efficient approvals, sustainable financing, stronger governance, greater adoption of technology and continued investment in skilled human capital. Above all, we need confidence. Sri Lanka needs housing. It needs infrastructure. It needs modern commercial development. It needs foreign investment and productive employment opportunities for young people. A strong and responsible construction industry contributes to all of these objectives. The challenges remain significant, but the opportunity is greater. As business leaders, our responsibility is not merely to identify difficulties or wait for economic conditions to improve. It is to find solutions, improve efficiency, protect customer and investor confidence, complete what we have started and continue investing in the country’s future. With disciplined private-sector leadership and a stable, investment-friendly policy environment, Sri Lanka’s construction and property sector can move beyond recovery and become a powerful contributor to investment, employment and sustainable economic growth. The question is no longer simply how we overcome the challenges facing construction. The greater question is how we use this period to build a stronger industry—and through that industry, help build a stronger Sri Lanka. (The author is Group Chairman/CEO, Blue Ocean Group of Companies)

audit.headline: Red Notice Suspect in Triple Murder Case Brought Back to Sri Lanka
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); Anusha Lakmali, also known as Achini, who was the subject of an international Red Notice in connection with the murders of Aruna Vidanagamage, alias Meegasare Kajja, and his two children, has been brought back to Sri Lanka. The suspect was escorted to the country by a team from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID). She was brought to Sri Lanka from the United Arab Emirates. Further investigations relating to the suspect are expected to be conducted by the Criminal Investigation Department. Two other suspects linked to the triple murder, alleged organised crime figures Thembili Lahiru and Backhoe Saman, were previously brought back to Sri Lanka after being located overseas.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); Anusha Lakmali, also known as Achini, who was the subject of an international Red Notice in connection with the murders of Aruna Vidanagamage, alias Meegasare Kajja, and his two children, has been brought back to Sri Lanka. The suspect was escorted to the country by a team from the Criminal Investigation Department (CID). She was brought to Sri Lanka from the United Arab Emirates. Further investigations relating to the suspect are expected to be conducted by the Criminal Investigation Department. Two other suspects linked to the triple murder, alleged organised crime figures Thembili Lahiru and Backhoe Saman, were previously brought back to Sri Lanka after being located overseas. Aruna Vidanagamage, alias Meegasare Kajja, and his two children were shot dead on the night of February 18 last year in a triple murder that drew widespread attention and remains under investigation.

audit.headline: Thousands Impacted As Heavy Rains Batter 12 Districts Across Sri Lanka
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); A powerful spell of adverse weather continues to grip Sri Lanka, affecting more than 12,000 people across 12 districts, forcing families into safety centres, triggering landslide warnings, raising flood risks and prompting the closure of all schools across the country. According to the Disaster Management Centre, the prevailing heavy rainfall has impacted the districts of Colombo, Gampaha, Jaffna, Kalutara, Ampara, Kandy, Kurunegala, Matara, Puttalam, Ratnapura, Mannar and Trincomalee. A total of 12,032 people from 3,162 families have been affected by the severe weather conditions. Authorities said 304 people are currently being sheltered at eight safe locations. One death has also been reported from Madampe in Puttalam after a drowning incident. The victim was identified as a 56-year-old man.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); A powerful spell of adverse weather continues to grip Sri Lanka, affecting more than 12,000 people across 12 districts, forcing families into safety centres, triggering landslide warnings, raising flood risks and prompting the closure of all schools across the country. According to the Disaster Management Centre, the prevailing heavy rainfall has impacted the districts of Colombo, Gampaha, Jaffna, Kalutara, Ampara, Kandy, Kurunegala, Matara, Puttalam, Ratnapura, Mannar and Trincomalee. A total of 12,032 people from 3,162 families have been affected by the severe weather conditions. Authorities said 304 people are currently being sheltered at eight safe locations. One death has also been reported from Madampe in Puttalam after a drowning incident. The victim was identified as a 56-year-old man. Since October 23, partial damage has been reported to 227 houses, while two homes have been completely destroyed due to the adverse weather. The Department of Meteorology says the rainy conditions affecting the southwestern parts of the island are expected to continue today. Meteorologists noted that Cyclone "Arnab", which had been located over the west-central Bay of Bengal, has further intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm. As of 2.30 a.m. today (27), the system was located approximately 890 kilometres northeast of Kankesanthurai. The cyclone is forecast to move west-northwestward until 5.30 p.m. today (27) before making landfall over the Andhra Pradesh coast of India tomorrow morning. Although the system is not expected to directly impact Sri Lanka, weather officials say the strong airflow being drawn toward the cyclone is continuing to fuel the ongoing wet weather across the island. As a result, intermittent rain is expected in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern and North Western Provinces, as well as in the Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts. The Department of Meteorology has also advised the fishing and naval communities not to venture into the deep and shallow sea areas of the Bay of Bengal until further notice due to the prevailing conditions. Meanwhile, the highest rainfall recorded during the 24-hour period ending at 3.00 a.m. today was reported from Pooneryn in Kilinochchi, which received 163 millimetres of rain. Iluppaikkadavai in Mannar recorded 148 millimetres, while Tholpuram and Meesalai in Jaffna received 110 millimetres and 101 millimetres respectively. Amid the continuing downpours, red evacuation notices over landslide risks have been issued for several Divisional Secretariat divisions in the districts of Ratnapura, Nuwara Eliya and Kalutara. In Ratnapura District, the affected divisions are Ratnapura, Ayagama, Pelmadulla, Kuruwita, Elapatha and Opanayake. Red landslide notices have also been issued for Bulathsinhala and Dodangoda in Kalutara District and Ambagamuwa Korale and Norwood in Nuwara Eliya District. Level Two landslide warnings have meanwhile been issued for Attanagalla in Gampaha District; Agalawatta, Walallawita, Millaniya, Palindanuwara, Ingiriya, Madurawala and Matugama in Kalutara District; Udunuwara, Pasbage Korale, Ganga Ihala Korale, Udapalatha and Yatinuwara in Kandy District; Kegalle, Ruwanwella, Mawanella, Rambukkana, Dehiowita, Aranayake, Galigamuwa, Deraniyagala, Yatiyantota, Bulathkohupitiya and Warakapola in Kegalle District; and Kurunegala Divisional Secretariat Division in Kurunegala District. Additional Level Two warnings have been issued for Kotmale East and West in Nuwara Eliya District and Nivithigala, Kiriella, Balangoda, Godakawela, Eheliyagoda and Kalawana in Ratnapura District. Level One landslide warnings remain active in several other Divisional Secretariat divisions across the districts of Galle, Gampaha, Kalutara, Kandy, Kegalle, Kurunegala, Nuwara Eliya and Ratnapura. The Irrigation Department says the Kalu Ganga, Nilwala Ganga and Attanagalu Oya are currently at minor flood levels. The Kalu Ganga has reached minor flood levels at Ratnapura and Millakanda, while the Nilwala Ganga has reached a similar status at Panadugama. The Attanagalu Oya is also flowing at minor flood level near Dunamale. In addition, the Kelani, Gin, Maha Oya and Deduru Oya rivers remain at flood-risk levels, according to Director of the Hydrology Division, Engineer L.S. Sooriyabandara. Heavy rainfall has also pushed 30 tanks and reservoirs into spill level. The Irrigation Department said major reservoirs including Deduru Oya, Rajanganaya, Thabbowa, Inginimitiya and Kala Wewa are currently overflowing. With the severe weather expected to continue, authorities have ordered the closure of all schools across Sri Lanka today. Deputy Minister of Education Dr. Madhura Seneviratne said the practical examinations for the Aesthetic Studies subject of the G.C.E. Ordinary Level Examination will proceed as scheduled. All pre-schools across the island have also been ordered closed today. Meanwhile, the public has been urged to contact 117 or the National Disaster Relief Services Centre hotline on 071 680 7807 during any emergency situation. Deputy Minister of Defence Major General (Retd.) Aruna Jayasekara said operations rooms at all three Tri-Forces headquarters have been activated and are on standby to respond immediately to any disaster situation that may arise as the country remains on alert over the evolving weather emergency.

audit.headline: Gymmaxxing, Sleepmaxxing, AI Maxxing: The Trend That Defined 2026
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); If 2026 felt like a year of constantly trying to do more, be more and get more out of life, there is now a word for it. Dictionary.com has named"maxxing" its Word of the Year for 2026, recognising a term that has exploded from internet slang into a global cultural phenomenon. The selection reflects a year in which people increasingly sought to optimise every aspect of their lives, from fitness and sleep to careers, technology and personal wellbeing. Derived from the word "maximizing," maxxing refers to pursuing an activity to the fullest or optimising a particular aspect of life as much as possible. audit.headline: Thirty Thousand Indian Fishing Boats Return to Indian Shores Amid Cyclone Arnab Threat
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st): More than 30,000 Indian fishing boats that had gone out to sea have returned to ports in Andhra Pradesh amid Cyclone Arnab, according to reports. Red alerts have been issued for seven districts in Andhra Pradesh. The cyclone was located approximately 650 kilometres southeast of Visakhapatnam in the state early this morning (27). India’s Meteorological Department says the cyclone is expected to severely affect five states, including Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh, today (27), tomorrow (28) and the day after (29). Indian media reports say heavy rainfall is also affecting Tamil Nadu due to Cyclone Arnab and the northeast monsoon. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu has already allocated 270 crore Indian rupees for disaster relief operations. Authorities have also closed schools in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, according to foreign media reports.

audit.headline: Can Football Become Sri Lanka's No.1 Sport in Just Four Years? FIFA Thinks So
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); A meeting in Azerbaijan could mark the beginning of the biggest transformation Sri Lankan football has seen in decades. FIFA President Gianni Infantino met Sri Lanka's Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports, Sunil Kumara Gamage, and Football Federation of Sri Lanka President Jaswar Umar in Baku to discuss an ambitious roadmap aimed at making football the country's most popular sport within the next four years. The discussions focused on a comprehensive development programme that would expand football opportunities across Sri Lanka, modernise infrastructure and create a stronger pathway for young players to reach the highest levels of the game. Sharing details of the meeting, Infantino said FIFA is eager to support Sri Lanka's football ambitions and help unlock the potential that exists across the island.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); A meeting in Azerbaijan could mark the beginning of the biggest transformation Sri Lankan football has seen in decades. FIFA President Gianni Infantino met Sri Lanka's Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports, Sunil Kumara Gamage, and Football Federation of Sri Lanka President Jaswar Umar in Baku to discuss an ambitious roadmap aimed at making football the country's most popular sport within the next four years. The discussions focused on a comprehensive development programme that would expand football opportunities across Sri Lanka, modernise infrastructure and create a stronger pathway for young players to reach the highest levels of the game. Sharing details of the meeting, Infantino said FIFA is eager to support Sri Lanka's football ambitions and help unlock the potential that exists across the island. "I held a constructive meeting with a delegation from Sri Lanka, including Sports Minister Sunil Kumara Gamage, Football Federation of Sri Lanka President Jaswar Umar, National Sports Council Chairman Priyantha Ekanayake, and High Performance Centre lead Prasanna Jayalath." "We spoke about supporting infrastructure projects and collaborating with the government and the Football Federation of Sri Lanka on development initiatives. I am excited to work in partnership to ensure the passion for football, talent and potential in this beautiful island nation find the right opportunities and pathways." "Events such as the ongoing FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival will only help in this regard, helping children showcase and hone their skills while experiencing the pride of representing their country on a global stage." During the discussions, Minister Sunil Kumara Gamage expressed the Sri Lankan Government's appreciation for FIFA's continued support towards the development of the national team and youth football programmes, while reaffirming the government's commitment to accelerating the growth of the sport across the country. A key feature of the proposed programme is a significant financial commitment from FIFA, with approximately US$25 million expected to be made available over the next four-year cycle to support the national team, youth development, women's football, coaches and referees. The talks also placed major emphasis on infrastructure development, including plans for a state-of-the-art international football stadium and an islandwide expansion of football facilities. One of the most ambitious proposals discussed was the construction of football grounds in every district, with work expected to begin next year. Complementing that initiative, the Football Federation of Sri Lanka plans to develop approximately 40 football grounds through its member leagues by the end of 2031, dramatically increasing access to the sport for children, youth and communities across the country. The meeting also explored the establishment of a National High-Performance Centre, with FIFA expected to provide technical expertise and infrastructure support in partnership with the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and the Football Federation of Sri Lanka. The proposed facility is expected to play a crucial role in player development, coaching excellence and creating professional pathways for talented Sri Lankan athletes. The discussions highlighted a growing partnership between FIFA, the Sri Lankan Government and the Football Federation of Sri Lanka, centred on expanding participation, improving facilities and raising the overall standard of football nationwide. For Sri Lankan football fans, the vision emerging from Baku is a bold one: more football grounds, better facilities, stronger youth programmes, increased international support and a long-term goal of taking the sport into every community while making football the nation's favourite game within four years.

audit.headline: Namal Rajapaksa Produced Before Hulftsdorp Magistrate’s Court
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News1st): Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organizer and Member of Parliament Namal Rajapaksa, who is currently in remand custody, was brought to the Hulftsdorp Magistrate’s Court this morning. He was produced before the court in connection with a case filed by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over the alleged acceptance of a Rs. 100 million bribe relating to the Airbus deal. When the case was taken up on October 13, the Attorney General informed the court that investigations into the matter had been concluded. Accordingly, the suspect had been remanded until today.

audit.headline: Environmentalists celebrate Lula’s reelection in Brazil: ‘The Amazon can breathe a sigh of relief’
audit.summary: Environmentalists, Indigenous groups and climate scientists are celebrating the reelection in Brazil of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , which brings the prospect of a continued focus on stopping the illegal cutting of the Amazon, the largest rainforest in the world. But supporters also warned that a Congress increasingly dominated by the far right and the agribusiness caucus could undermine those efforts to protect the forest and combat climate change . Lula defeated Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, son of far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro, in Sunday’s runoff with 51.78% of the vote to 48.21%. After trailing in the first round, Lula staged a comeback to win by 4.4 million votes. “The Amazon can breathe a sigh of relief!” said David Lapola, a Brazilian scientist and lead author of a chapter on so-called tipping points in an upcoming United Nations climate report.
audit.body: Environmentalists, Indigenous groups and climate scientists are celebrating the reelection in Brazil of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , which brings the prospect of a continued focus on stopping the illegal cutting of the Amazon, the largest rainforest in the world. But supporters also warned that a Congress increasingly dominated by the far right and the agribusiness caucus could undermine those efforts to protect the forest and combat climate change . Lula defeated Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, son of far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro, in Sunday’s runoff with 51.78% of the vote to 48.21%. After trailing in the first round, Lula staged a comeback to win by 4.4 million votes. “The Amazon can breathe a sigh of relief!” said David Lapola, a Brazilian scientist and lead author of a chapter on so-called tipping points in an upcoming United Nations climate report. Scientists debate the threshold beyond which the dense, humid Amazon rainforest could shift to a drier ecosystem, with irreversible consequences for biodiversity and the climate. The forest absorbs vast amounts of carbon dioxide, a greenhouse gas that drives global warming. About 60% of the Amazon lies in Brazil. Lula’s victory reflected shifts in voter support and higher turnout nationwide. In the Amazon, Indigenous communities and advocacy groups mobilized voters and, aided by court rulings last week, helped secure government transportation for those living in remote areas. The Articulation of Indigenous Peoples of Brazil, known as APIB, was among the organizations that went to court to secure Indigenous voters’ access to the polls. Lula’s victory reflected the “strength of grassroots mobilization in defense of democracy, life and Indigenous peoples’ rights,” it said in a statement. Flávio Bolsonaro refused to concede Monday and said he would ask the electoral court to nullify the results. He faces a high hurdle: presenting evidence of fraud sufficient to overturn Lula’s winning margin and persuading the court before the results are certified Dec. 18. Early signals from Brazil’s institutions and regional leaders, including conservative presidents who oppose Lula, suggest the outcome will be accepted at home and abroad. Flávio Bolsonaro had pledged to pursue policies aligned with those of his father, who governed from 2019 through 2022. Deforestation surged under Jair Bolsonaro as his administration weakened environmental enforcement agencies and loosened regulations. Lula’s government last week announced the lowest Amazon deforestation rate on record. Lula is expected to continue efforts to curb deforestation and finance a sustainable economy through international donations as well as public and private funding. While he was the clear favorite for environmentalists, climate scientists and others who want to protect the Amazon, Lula has put forward policies that have drawn criticism. Most recently, he has supported efforts to drill for oil in offshore waters near the Amazon. Still, Flávio Bolsonaro presented a stark choice that for many environmentalists felt would put the Amazon and Brazil’s overall environmental protections at risk. He had denied climate change while casting himself as an environmental defender. However, he offered few details on forest protection or financing, calling for “modernizing” environmental laws and giving Amazon landowners more decision-making power — proposals environmentalists warned could weaken safeguards and accelerate deforestation. AP

audit.headline: Four of 17 Undertrials who Escaped From Tamil Nadu Jail Recaptured, 13 Still at Large
audit.summary: Tamil Nadu Police have recaptured four of the 17 undertrial prisoners who escaped from the Thekkampatti sub-jail near Andipatti in Tamil Nadu’s Theni district, while a manhunt is underway to trace the remaining 13. The escape took place at around 11.20 pm, local time in India, according to police officials cited by Indian Media. The inmates allegedly staged a medical emergency to trick prison guards into opening their cell before overpowering the staff and fleeing the facility. One of the prisoners reportedly pretended to suffer an epileptic seizure while sharing a cell with other inmates. When guards unlocked the door to provide medical assistance, the prisoners allegedly attacked them, overpowering the personnel in a brief struggle. Three prison staff members were injured in the incident.
audit.body: Tamil Nadu Police have recaptured four of the 17 undertrial prisoners who escaped from the Thekkampatti sub-jail near Andipatti in Tamil Nadu’s Theni district, while a manhunt is underway to trace the remaining 13. The escape took place at around 11.20 pm, local time in India, according to police officials cited by Indian Media. The inmates allegedly staged a medical emergency to trick prison guards into opening their cell before overpowering the staff and fleeing the facility. One of the prisoners reportedly pretended to suffer an epileptic seizure while sharing a cell with other inmates. When guards unlocked the door to provide medical assistance, the prisoners allegedly attacked them, overpowering the personnel in a brief struggle. Three prison staff members were injured in the incident. Grade II Police Constable Thangapandi suffered serious head injuries and was taken to the Government Hospital at G Vilakku for treatment. Two other personnel sustained minor injuries. All 17 inmates managed to escape from the facility following the assault. Police identified the four recaptured prisoners as Praveen Kumar, Silambarasan, Raja Sikandar and Rajkumar. Inspector General of Police (South Zone) Vijayendra Bidari has formed 17 special teams to track down the fugitives. Vehicle checks have been intensified in neighbouring Dindigul district, while police in Kerala have also been alerted. Combing operations are underway in forest areas along the Western Ghats and in Idukki district. Source: Firstpost | The Indian Express

audit.headline: Cargills Bank introduces country’s first Ocean Plastic Debit Card
audit.summary: Cargills Bank has launched the Cargills Bank Ocean Plastic Debit Card, marking the first time such a product has been introduced to the Sri Lankan market. This initiative is a key part of the bank’s commitment to sustainable banking and serves as a practical step toward addressing the global challenge of marine pollution. The cards are produced using recycled ocean-bound plastic specifically sourced from the Indian Ocean region, including the Maldives, as well as the Dominican Republic. By transitioning to these recycled materials, Cargills Bank aims to raise meaningful awareness about the impact of plastic waste on our oceans while supporting the protection of coastal ecosystems.
audit.body: Cargills Bank has launched the Cargills Bank Ocean Plastic Debit Card, marking the first time such a product has been introduced to the Sri Lankan market.  This initiative is a key part of the bank’s commitment to sustainable banking and serves as a practical step toward addressing the global challenge of marine pollution.  The cards are produced using recycled ocean-bound plastic specifically sourced from the Indian Ocean region, including the Maldives, as well as the Dominican Republic.  By transitioning to these recycled materials, Cargills Bank aims to raise meaningful awareness about the impact of plastic waste on our oceans while supporting the protection of coastal ecosystems. This move aligns the bank’s operations with circular economy principles, providing customers with a way to support environmental sustainability through their everyday financial choices. Commenting on the launch, Senarath Bandara, Managing Director / CEO of Cargills Bank said, “This sustainability initiative is a continuation of the bank’s Corporate Sustainability Goals (CSG), reflecting a deep-seated commitment to reducing the environmental footprint of traditional banking operations. The successful realization of this eco-friendly product was made possible through the technical and production expertise of Lake House Printers and Publishers PLC, alongside the global payment technology leadership of Mastercard. Together, these partners have ensured that the Ocean Plastic card meets the highest international standards of durability and security while remaining an emblem of environmental responsibility.” Adding to the operational vision of the product, Shihan Pathiraja, Chief Manager - Cards Services of Cargills Bank, noted: “From an operational standpoint, transitioning to ocean-bound plastic was a meticulous process to ensure that sustainability did not compromise functional excellence.  We have integrated this eco-friendly material into our existing debit card infrastructure seamlessly, ensuring that our customers enjoy the same high-speed transaction capabilities and global acceptance they expect from Cargills Bank. This product allows our cardholders to carry a piece of our conservation mission in their pockets, turning every point-of-sale interaction into a statement of environmental advocacy.” To further drive awareness and community engagement, Cargills Bank will be providing extensive visibility for this initiative across its social media channels, inviting customers to become active participants in the bank’s journey toward a greener future.  This launch underscores the bank’s belief that modern financial services must not only be innovative but also ethically aligned with the preservation of the planet for future generations.

audit.headline: American Premium Water’s ‘Fill Her Glass’ wins Gold at Dragons of Asia 2026
audit.summary: American Premium Water, a pioneer in Sri Lanka’s bottled drinking water industry for 30 years, has earned regional recognition for its commitment to sustainability and purpose-led communication. Its World Water Day campaign, ‘Fill Her Glass’, won a Gold Dragon in Cause, Environment or Sustainability and a Black Dragon in Small Budget at the Dragons of Asia Awards in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. The campaign was also nominated as finalist for the Red Dragon, recognising the Best in Asia. The achievement reflects American Premium Water’s belief that sustainability extends beyond environmental responsibility to encompass social progress, inclusion and equal opportunity.
audit.body: American Premium Water, a pioneer in Sri Lanka’s bottled drinking water industry for 30 years, has earned regional recognition for its commitment to sustainability and purpose-led communication.  Its World Water Day campaign, ‘Fill Her Glass’, won a Gold Dragon in Cause, Environment or Sustainability and a Black Dragon in Small Budget at the Dragons of Asia Awards in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.  The campaign was also nominated as finalist for the Red Dragon, recognising the Best in Asia. The achievement reflects American Premium Water’s belief that sustainability extends beyond environmental responsibility to encompass social progress, inclusion and equal opportunity. Through ‘Fill Her Glass,’ the company highlighted the often-overlooked challenges faced by women and girls in communities where access to water is limited, and how the burden of water collection can affect education, livelihoods and quality of life. At the heart of the campaign is the thought, “She fills the world, but her glass is empty.” This powerful insight highlights that reliable access to water is about more than meeting an essential need. It can also give women and girls more time, freedom and opportunity to pursue their ambitions and shape their futures. American Premium Water CEO Fayaz Fazal said, “Having pioneered bottled drinking water in Sri Lanka and led the industry for 30 years, we recognise that our responsibility goes beyond providing access to quality drinking water. Sustainability also means understanding the wider impact water has on people, communities and opportunity. Through ‘Fill Her Glass,’ we wanted to shine a light on the challenges faced by women and girls and encourage a more meaningful conversation about water access and equality.  We are proud to see a campaign from Sri Lanka recognised on the Asian stage. This reinforces our commitment to using our brand and platform to champion causes that matter and contribute to a more sustainable and equitable future.” The Dragons of Asia recognition adds to a strong run of accolades for American Premium Water’s recent marketing and communications initiatives. At the Dragons of Sri Lanka, the company secured four awards, including three Gold Dragons and one Black Dragon. It also won at SLIM Digis 2.6 in the category of Cross Media Integration. The success of ‘Fill Her Glass’ reflects the collaborative efforts of American Premium Water and its communications partner, Shift Solutions, whose creativity and strategic partnership helped bring the campaign to life.  Together, these accolades demonstrate American Premium Water’s focus on combining creative thinking, strategic communication and purpose to strengthen its brand while bringing important social and sustainability issues into the public conversation. As a pioneer in Sri Lanka’s bottled water industry, American Premium Water continues to champion a broader understanding of sustainability, recognising the connection between access to essential resources, community wellbeing and a more equitable future.

audit.headline: Home Lands Group breaks ground on Diamond Tower, its new headquarters in Colombo

The groundbreaking and foundation stone laying ceremony was led by Nalin Herath, Chairman and Managing Director, whose vision has guided the Group for almost two and a half decades to its position today as Sri Lanka’s No. 1, most trusted and most innovative developer.He was joined bythe directors,management, staff and distinguished guests. Together, they broke ground and laid the foundation stone, a moment that reflected the Group’s shared vision and the strength of the leadership team that will carry the Group into its next era of growth. Rising 21 floors above three basement levels, Home Lands Diamond Tower is set to become a bold new landmark in Colombo’s skyline.
audit.body: Home Lands Group of Companies marked a defining milestone, breaking ground on Home Lands Diamond Tower, the Group’s new corporate headquarters in Thummulla, Colombo.  The groundbreaking and foundation stone laying ceremony was led by Nalin Herath, Chairman and Managing Director, whose vision has guided the Group for almost two and a half decades to its position today as Sri Lanka’s No. 1, most trusted and most innovative developer.He was joined bythe directors,management, staff and distinguished guests.  Together, they broke ground and laid the foundation stone, a moment that reflected the Group’s shared vision and the strength of the leadership team that will carry the Group into its next era of growth. Rising 21 floors above three basement levels, Home Lands Diamond Tower is set to become a bold new landmark in Colombo’s skyline. Inspired by the brilliance and strength of a diamond, the tower’s futuristic design features a distinctive diamond-patterned façade and a signature diamond-shaped crown, giving it an iconic presence in the city.  Conceived as a building of the future, it will combine intelligent design, advanced building technology and modern, dynamic workspaces to create an environment built for innovation, collaboration, excellence and will serve as the Group’s flagship address as it continues to shape the future of Sri Lankan real estate. The tower will be built by Heyraa Construction, the Group’s own construction arm, which holdsthe highest CS2 grading from the Construction Industry Development Authority (CIDA). Scheduled for completion in thirty months, the project will showcase the engineering capability and uncompromising quality that define every Home Lands development. “Diamond Tower is a statement of where Home Lands is heading. Trust has always been our foundation, innovation is our driving force, and excellence is our standard. From here, we will lead the next generation of real estate, creating developments that set new benchmarks for how people live, work and invest,” said Nalin Herath. Today, Home Lands stands as a real estate conglomerate of 14 specialized companies working in synergy to deliver end-to-end solutions in real estate, construction, property management and lifestyle creation, with international offices in Australia, Dubai and London.  Backed by a strong leadership team, sound governance and a proven track record of delivery, the Group has built a solid foundation of trust with all stakeholders. Diamond Tower reflects the scale of this growth and strengthens the Group’s corporate presence as it expands its reach.More than a corporate address, Home Lands Diamond Tower marks the beginning of a new chapter for the Group. It will stand as a lasting symbol of the ambition, resilience and trust that have shaped its success. Home Lands is the pioneer of resort-style residential developments in Sri Lanka. The market leader has sold over 5,000 units across 24 large-scale development projects, of which over 3,750 units have already been delivered.  Home Lands has won the Best Developer – Sri Lanka award at the PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards three times (2021, 2024 and 2025). In 2025, it became the only real estate developer in Sri Lanka to be recognised as a Superbrand.  As a fully integrated group of 14 companies, including its own construction arm, Home Lands delivers end-to-end solutions built on quality, innovation and customer satisfaction.

audit.headline: Sri Lanka Determined to Stay Off Global Financial Watchlists, Says PM
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka's Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya warned that corruption remains one of the biggest threats not only to economic stability but also to the stability of a nation itself. Addressing Sri Lanka's third mutual evaluation by the Asia-Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG), the Prime Minister said the strength of a country's financial system depends not only on institutions and regulations, but on how effectively they work together in practice. She described the mutual evaluation as a significant milestone for Sri Lanka, saying it provides an opportunity for the country to demonstrate its commitment to combating money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing, while also highlighting the progress achieved through years of collective institutional effort.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka's Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya warned that corruption remains one of the biggest threats not only to economic stability but also to the stability of a nation itself. Addressing Sri Lanka's third mutual evaluation by the Asia-Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG), the Prime Minister said the strength of a country's financial system depends not only on institutions and regulations, but on how effectively they work together in practice. She described the mutual evaluation as a significant milestone for Sri Lanka, saying it provides an opportunity for the country to demonstrate its commitment to combating money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing, while also highlighting the progress achieved through years of collective institutional effort. The Prime Minister stressed that a strong anti-money laundering and counter-terrorism financing framework is vital to protecting the integrity of the financial system, safeguarding the economy from illicit activities and maintaining the confidence of international partners, investors and financial institutions. However, she noted that the challenge facing countries today extends beyond financial regulation. "One of the major crises that democratic nations across the world are experiencing currently is the erosion of trust in public institutions, particularly in institutions that are expected to govern and also in financial institutions." The Prime Minister said corruption lies at the heart of that crisis. "The major reason for this is corruption. Unless we deal with this, this is actually a real threat not just to economic stability but to political stability and the stability of a nation in general." Recalling Sri Lanka's previous experiences under increased monitoring by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), Dr. Amarasuriya said those periods carried significant consequences for the country's reputation, financial sector and broader economic prospects. "We are mindful of the lessons we have learned from the past. Sri Lanka has twice experienced the challenges associated with being placed under the Financial Action Task Force increased monitoring. Those experiences had far-reaching implications for the country's reputation, financial sector and economic prospects." She said the experiences point to the need for a strong and effective anti-money laundering, counter-terrorism financing and counter-proliferation financing regime, backed by sustained commitment across all institutions. The Prime Minister said the Government's objective is clear. "Today our objective is clear. To demonstrate the strength of our systems, sustain the progress we have achieved and ensure that Sri Lanka remains a trusted and responsible member of the global financial community." Dr. Amarasuriya stressed that the Government's commitment extends beyond the evaluation itself. "Let me assure you that the government of Sri Lanka remains fully committed to the success of this process and to the continuous strengthening of this regime, the anti-corruption regime, not any other regime." She said the country's broader vision is centred on transparency, good governance, financial integrity and sustainable economic growth, noting that Sri Lanka has implemented substantial legislative, regulatory, supervisory, investigative and enforcement reforms over the years. According to the Prime Minister, the benefits of those reforms are already becoming visible, particularly over the last two years. She credited the progress to a coordinated whole-of-government approach involving policymakers, regulators, supervisors, law enforcement agencies, the judiciary, reporting institutions and private sector stakeholders. Describing the evaluation as an opportunity for reflection as well as assessment, Dr. Amarasuriya said Sri Lanka remains committed to identifying weaknesses and strengthening areas that require improvement. She noted that recommendations emerging from the evaluation would help the country further align its systems with international best practices while addressing emerging risks more effectively.

The platform provides new Wealth Planners the essential knowledge and capabilities required to begin their careers with AIA.
audit.body: AIA Sri Lanka has launched iAcademy, a next-generation digital learning platform designed to simplify and modernise the onboarding and training experience for new Wealth Planners, marking another significant milestone in the company’s transformation journey through Project NOVA. Designed to make learning more accessible and engaging, iAcademy transforms traditionally location-based training programmes into a digital experience that can be accessed online, anytime and anywhere. AIA Wealth Planners can now progress through their training at their own pace while benefiting from a consistent and structured onboarding experience. The platform provides new Wealth Planners the essential knowledge and capabilities required to begin their careers with AIA. The learning journey includes an introduction to values and culture, together with comprehensive product knowledge, insurance fundamentals, an understanding of the Wealth Planner profession and its benefits, sales processes and best practices, and compliance and regulatory requirements. iAcademy also includes an interactive orientation learning experience, licensing examination guidance, with trilingual language support. Importantly, the platform goes beyond digital learning to help streamline the wider onboarding journey. iAcademy provides real-time visibility of training progress and completion status, and upon the successful completion of all required modules, the onboarding process is automatically advanced. Commenting on the launch, Upul Wijesinghe, Deputy Chief Executive Officer/Chief Distribution Officer (CDO) of AIA Sri Lanka, said, “By harnessing technology, we are creating a faster, simpler and more accessible onboarding experience that gives our Wealth Planners greater flexibility in how they learn, while equipping them with the knowledge and confidence they need to succeed from day one.”  Dimuthu Piyasena, Chief Agency Officer of AIA Sri Lanka, added, “Our Wealth Planners are central to the way we connect with and serve our customers. iAcademy allows us to deliver a structured and engaging learning experience while giving new Wealth Planners the flexibility to learn at their own pace.”

audit.headline: SLID and ACCA announce second National Director Awards
audit.summary: Dinesh Weerakkody Anitra Perera Nilusha Ranasinghe Following the success of the inaugural National Director Awards, the Sri Lanka Institute of Directors (SLID), in collaboration with the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) announced the return of the SLID–ACCA National Director Awards for its second year. Applications opened on 23 October and will close on 30 November, culminating in the National Director Awards ceremony on 10 February 2027. Established as a national platform to recognise outstanding directorship, the Awards celebrate individuals whose leadership, governance and stewardship make a measurable contribution to their organisations, stakeholders and the wider economy.
audit.body: Dinesh Weerakkody Anitra Perera Nilusha Ranasinghe Following the success of the inaugural National Director Awards, the Sri Lanka Institute of Directors (SLID), in collaboration with the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) announced the return of the SLID–ACCA National Director Awards for its second year. Applications opened on 23 October and will close on 30 November, culminating in the National Director Awards ceremony on 10 February 2027. Established as a national platform to recognise outstanding directorship, the Awards celebrate individuals whose leadership, governance and stewardship make a measurable contribution to their organisations, stakeholders and the wider economy. In a significant expansion of its scope, the 2026/27 SLID–ACCA National Director Awards will introduce three new award categories, marking an important milestone in recognising excellence in governance across Sri Lanka’s public and private sectors.  The Best Governed Organisation Award will recognise organisations demonstrating exceptional corporate governance, board effectiveness and accountability, while the Excellence in Public Sector Governance Award will honour public institutions and state-owned enterprises setting benchmarks in transparency, responsible stewardship and public value creation. The Public Sector Leadership Award will recognise outstanding individual leadership and contributions to strengthening governance within the public sector. For the first time, the Awards will recognise both individual directors and organisations, reinforcing their position as a national platform for celebrating and advancing excellence in governance, leadership and boardroom practices. Dinesh Weerakkody, Chairman of SLID said, “Strong boards are the foundation of strong institutions, resilient businesses and a competitive economy. Through the SLID–ACCA National Director Awards, we seek to elevate the importance of effective board leadership and recognise directors who are making a meaningful contribution to advancing corporate governance standards across Sri Lanka” Anitra Perera, Chief Executive Officer of SLID emphasized, “More than recognition, the Awards are about setting higher standards for the future of Sri Lanka’s boardrooms. We strongly encourage directors and organisations across Sri Lanka to participate, put forward those making a real difference in the boardroom, and help us recognise the leadership that is shaping the future of governance in our country.” Nilusha Ranasinghe, Head of ACCA South Asia added, “ACCA is committed to championing responsible leadership and sustainable business practices, recognising that long-term prosperity is built on transparency, accountability, ethical decision-making and strong governance. Our collaboration with SLID reflects our shared commitment to equipping and inspiring directors to lead with both financial insight and purpose—strengthening organisations and creating sustainable value for business and society.”

audit.headline: Mixed tones mark week’s start

Moving along the belly, the 01.12.2031 bond traded at 11.85 percent, followed by the 15.12.2032 maturity at 12.00 percent.

Integrating digital convenience with operational efficiency, SLT-MOBITEL is actively helping reshape the country’s transport ecosystem for the future.   The Stakeholders Engagement & Recognition Event was held recently at Amari Colombo, with key figures from the transport ecosystem in attendance, strengthening collaboration, celebrating achievements, and exploring the future of digital bus ticketing.  The event was graced by Prasanna Gunasena, Deputy Minister of Transport. SLT-MOBITEL Senior Management, alongside long-distance and highway bus operators, were also in attendance.    As the digital platform provider, SLT-MOBITEL is amplifying the infrastructure of www.busticket.gov.lk, powering the platform to deliver a reliable, efficient, and accessible online bus experience for passengers while supporting data-driven operations for transport authorities and bus operators.   The session featured platform performance highlights, success stories, the recognition of high-performing operators, and demonstrations of new capabilities while exploring opportunities to further expand digital adoption among bus operators nationwide.

audit.headline: Laugfs Gas explores partial or full exit from terminal subsidiary
audit.summary: Laugfs Gas yesterday said it is weighing a partial or full sale of its terminal subsidiary, with the preliminary talks also covering investment and commercial collaboration options. In a disclosure to the Colombo Stock Exchange the company said it was holding informal discussions with the interested parties on strategic options for its wholly-owned subsidiary Laugfs Terminals Limited. The subsidiary owns and operates the 30,000-metric-tonne liquefied petroleum gas terminal at the Hambantota International Port. A full disposal would see Laugfs Gas exit its shareholding in the terminal business. However, a sale remains one of several options under consideration, with no transaction agreed. The company said no agreement had been reached on the structure or terms of a transaction and no definitive transaction agreement had been signed.
