audit.headline: BOC plans debenture issue of up to Rs.30 billion
audit.summary: Bank of Ceylon (BOC) plans to raise up to Rs.30 billion through a listed debenture issue, offering five and seven-year instruments, with fixed or floating interest rates. The bank’s board has approved an initial issue of Rs.10 billion, with two options to raise a further Rs.10 billion each in the event of oversubscription, according to a disclosure to the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) dated October 26. Both increases will be at the bank’s discretion. The Basel III-compliant Tier 2 debentures will be issued at Rs.100 each. The CSE has granted an in-principle approval for the proposed issue. The five-year fixed-rate debentures will pay 12.75 percent annually, while the seven-year fixed-rate instruments will carry an annual interest rate of 13 percent.
audit.body: Bank of Ceylon (BOC) plans to raise up to Rs.30 billion through a listed debenture issue, offering five and seven-year instruments, with fixed or floating interest rates. The bank’s board has approved an initial issue of Rs.10 billion, with two options to raise a further Rs.10 billion each in the event of oversubscription, according to a disclosure to the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE) dated October 26. Both increases will be at the bank’s discretion. The Basel III-compliant Tier 2 debentures will be issued at Rs.100 each. The CSE has granted an in-principle approval for the proposed issue. The five-year fixed-rate debentures will pay 12.75 percent annually, while the seven-year fixed-rate instruments will carry an annual interest rate of 13 percent. The floating-rate investors will receive the 12-month treasury bill rate plus 1.50 percentage points for the five-year instruments and plus 1.75 percentage points for the seven-year instruments. The interest on all four categories will be paid annually. The issue carries an ‘AA (Stable)’ rating from Lanka Rating Agency Limited. The bank separately disclosed an issuer rating of ‘AA-(lka)’, with a stable outlook, from Fitch Ratings Lanka Limited. The subscriptions will be restricted to qualified investors. The individual investors must make an initial investment of at least Rs.5 million, while the minimum subscription for other qualified investors is Rs.10,000. The applications above the applicable minimum must be in multiples of Rs.10,000. The unsecured, subordinated debentures include non-viability write-down provisions, allowing the losses to be imposed on the investors’ principal at the sole discretion of the Central Bank’s Governing Board, without the debenture holders’ approval. The mechanism can be triggered if the Governing Board determines that a write-down is necessary to prevent the bank from becoming non-viable or if the public-sector capital or equivalent support is required to prevent that outcome.

audit.headline: Exporters seek support to meet new EU food and packaging rules
audit.summary: The Sri Lankan exporters are seeking technical assistance and training to meet the new European Union (EU) food safety and packaging requirements, with limits on certain mineral oil contaminants in food, scheduled to apply from January 2027. The National Chamber of Exporters of Sri Lanka (NCE) yesterday said it was working with the other stakeholders to secure support for the businesses preparing to comply with the requirements. A key concern is the EU’s new maximum levels for mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons (MOAH) in food. A European Commission statement set January 01, 2027 as the application date for most of the limits. Sri Lanka’s Commerce Department has also begun assessing the country’s readiness.
audit.body: The Sri Lankan exporters are seeking technical assistance and training to meet the new European Union (EU) food safety and packaging requirements, with limits on certain mineral oil contaminants in food, scheduled to apply from January 2027. The National Chamber of Exporters of Sri Lanka (NCE) yesterday said it was working with the other stakeholders to secure support for the businesses preparing to comply with the requirements. A key concern is the EU’s new maximum levels for mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons (MOAH) in food. A European Commission statement set January 01, 2027 as the application date for most of the limits. Sri Lanka’s Commerce Department has also begun assessing the country’s readiness. It convened a stakeholder meeting on September 24 to examine the preparations for the proposed MOAH regulation and highlighted the need for the exporters to respond to the evolving European market requirements. The NCE council also discussed the EU’s Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation, which has implications for the businesses supplying the European market. The regulation generally began applying on August 12, 2026 and covers packaging placed on the EU market, including imports from Sri Lanka. An EU-supported seminar held in Colombo in July sought to help the food exporters, packaging manufacturers, printers and other stakeholders prepare for the requirements.

audit.headline: Fitch assigns Asia Asset Finance’s proposed subordinated debt ‘A-(EXP)(lka)’
audit.summary: Fitch Ratings has assigned Asia Asset Finance PLC’s (AAF, A+(lka)/Stable) proposed Sri Lankan rupee-denominated subordinated listed debentures of up to Rs.3 billion an expected National Long-Term Rating of ‘A-(EXP)(lka)’. The proposed debentures are likely to have a five-year maturity and will be listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange. The company plans to use the proceeds to strengthen its Tier 2 capital base and support loan-book expansion. The final rating is subject to the receipt of final documentation conforming to the information already received. The proposed debentures are rated two notches below AAF’s National Long-Term Rating.
audit.body: Fitch Ratings has assigned Asia Asset Finance PLC’s (AAF, A+(lka)/Stable) proposed Sri Lankan rupee-denominated subordinated listed debentures of up to Rs.3 billion an expected National Long-Term Rating of ‘A-(EXP)(lka)’. The proposed debentures are likely to have a five-year maturity and will be listed on the Colombo Stock Exchange.  The company plans to use the proceeds to strengthen its Tier 2 capital base and support loan-book expansion. The final rating is subject to the receipt of final documentation conforming to the information already received. The proposed debentures are rated two notches below AAF’s National Long-Term Rating. Fitch applied the Bank Rating Criteria in rating this instrument, as it believes the prudential capital framework for Sri Lankan finance companies is closer to that for banks.  The expected rating reflects Fitch’s baseline notching for loss severity for this debt class and expectation of poor recoveries in the event of default. There is no additional notching for non-performance risk, as the proposed debentures do not contain going-concern loss-absorption features. AAF’s National Long-Term Rating reflects Fitch’s expectation that its majority shareholder, India-based Muthoot Finance Ltd (MFL, BB+/Stable), would provide extraordinary support to AAF if needed. This view is based on MFL’s 78.4 percent shareholding, record of ordinary equity support and the strategic and operational alignment between the parent and subsidiary in their core product - gold-backed loans.  Even so, Fitch assesses AAF’s strategic importance to MFL as limited, given the subsidiary’s small size, modest role and contribution, limited brand sharing and operations in a different jurisdiction.  AAF’s standalone credit profile does not drive the rating but Fitch assesses it as significantly weaker than its support-driven rating.

audit.headline: International Monetary Fund sees Sri Lanka primed for AI leapfrog
audit.summary: Shirin Hamid By Shabiya Ali Ahlam Sri Lanka has won praise from the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) technology chief for building the digital foundations to leapfrog into the artificial intelligence (AI) era, with a call to match the technological ambition with investment in people, sound judgment and accountability. “I think you are closer to this future than you think,” visiting IMF Chief Information Officer Shirin Hamid told the Central Bank of Sri Lanka’s (CBSL) 76th anniversary oration. Speaking on ‘The Intelligent Central Bank: Building Trust in the Age of AI’, Hamid highlighted Sri Lanka’s expanding digital payments, digital identity preparations and plans for secure data sharing as foundations for the next stage of transformation.
audit.body: Shirin Hamid By Shabiya Ali Ahlam Sri Lanka has won praise from the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) technology chief for building the digital foundations to leapfrog into the artificial intelligence (AI) era, with a call to match the technological ambition with investment in people, sound judgment and accountability. “I think you are closer to this future than you think,” visiting IMF Chief Information Officer Shirin Hamid told the Central Bank of Sri Lanka’s (CBSL) 76th anniversary oration. Speaking on ‘The Intelligent Central Bank: Building Trust in the Age of AI’, Hamid highlighted Sri Lanka’s expanding digital payments, digital identity preparations and plans for secure data sharing as foundations for the next stage of transformation. She opined Sri Lanka’s size need not constrain its ambitions as the smaller and newer institutions could have an advantage as AI tools become more accessible, allowing them to move ahead without the burden of decades-old technology. “You’re not dragging 50 years of legacy systems behind you,” Hamid said, highlighting cloud-native technology, open-source models and frugal AI as capabilities available to institutions of every size. “So, leapfrogging is not a slogan here; it is an option and it is yours to exercise but with judgment.” Hamid’s assessment placed Sri Lanka’s digital push within the broader effort to turn economic recovery into lasting institutional progress. She noted that the digital economy blueprint sought to make transformation a core pillar of recovery, through modernised public services, deeper financial innovation and greater private sector innovation. The deployment of digital public infrastructure, preparations for the national digital identity and development of a national data exchange platform to share information securely across the public and private institutions were among the initiatives she highlighted. Investment in the supporting foundations, including connectivity, skills and legal and policy frameworks, was also an investment in Sri Lanka’s AI preparedness, she said. “For every AI-influenced decision, we need a named human who is answerable,” she said. Hamid advocated giving institutions AI assistance before introducing autonomous agents, with greater independence granted only as systems proved themselves. “In other words, we should aim to augment judgment first and grant autonomy only where it has been earned.” She also urged the institutions to prepare for failure from the outset, maintaining backups, testing how AI systems could be manipulated and setting limits on the actions they could take. Such safeguards would help contain damage when the systems behaved incorrectly, particularly where their decisions could affect the market integrity or financial stability. Hamid said the challenge extended beyond any single technology. AI’s speed, the concentration of capabilities among a handful of model and cloud providers, uneven security capacity and governance that lagged behind technological progress together presented a formidable test. For the CBSL, the next task was to become an AI-augmented institution while protecting against those risks and preserving the trust restored through Sri Lanka’s recent difficulties. Hamid credited the CBSL with restoring trust under extraordinarily difficult circumstances, suggesting that achievement could now underpin its technological transition. “Sri Lanka has already shown that trust can be rebuilt,” she said. “We can now use AI to make trust stronger.”

audit.summary: Nine-month earnings top US $ 13.6bn September exports led by a 21.66% increase in merchandise earnings to US $ 1.39bn Services exports grew just 0.67% to an estimated US $ 306.17mn United States retained its position as Sri Lanka’s largest single export destination, with September shipments increasing 18.06% to US $ 281.84mn Sri Lanka’s exports posted a double-digit growth in September, with a sharp rise in the merchandise shipments lifting the total earnings to US $ 1.69 billion, although the nine-month performance remained weighed down by the declines in apparel and tea. The latest Export Development Board (EDB) figures showed the total exports rose 17.23 percent from September last year, led by a 21.66 percent increase in the merchandise earnings to US $ 1.39 billion. The services exports grew just 0.67 percent to an estimated US $ 306.17 million.
audit.body: Nine-month earnings top US $ 13.6bn September exports led by a 21.66% increase in merchandise earnings to US $ 1.39bn Services exports grew just 0.67% to an estimated US $ 306.17mn United States retained its position as Sri Lanka’s largest single export destination, with September shipments increasing 18.06% to US $ 281.84mn Sri Lanka’s exports posted a double-digit growth in September, with a sharp rise in the merchandise shipments lifting the total earnings to US $ 1.69 billion, although the nine-month performance remained weighed down by the declines in apparel and tea. The latest Export Development Board (EDB) figures showed the total exports rose 17.23 percent from September last year, led by a 21.66 percent increase in the merchandise earnings to US $ 1.39 billion. The services exports grew just 0.67 percent to an estimated US $ 306.17 million. The September performance helped push the cumulative exports to US $ 13.61 billion, up 5.04 percent year-on-year. The merchandise earnings increased 5.35 percent to US $ 10.76 billion, while services contributed US $ 2.85 billion, a gain of 3.88 percent. EDB Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Mangala Wijesinghe said the focus must now be on sustaining the growth and widening the export base. “Enhancing value addition, promoting innovation and technology adoption, diversifying export markets and integrating more deeply into global value chains will be essential to expanding the export earnings and generating greater economic value for the country,” he said. The strong gains in the electrical and electronic components, spices, rubber products and food and beverages helped offset the lower nine-month earnings from apparel and tea. Apparel and textiles recorded a September recovery, with the earnings rising 3.46 percent to US $ 439.78 million. The apparel exports alone grew 3.43 percent to US $ 408.69 million, supported by a 6.33 percent increase in the shipments to the United States. The apparel and textile exports fell 5.68 percent to US $ 3.78 billion in the first nine months, with the apparel earnings down 5.36 percent to US $ 3.51 billion. Over the nine months, the sector’s exports to the United States, European Union (EU) and United Kingdom declined by 3.83 percent, 5.54 percent and 10.41 percent, respectively. Tea also remained under pressure. The September earnings slipped 1.38 percent to US $ 135.11 million, taking the nine-month total to US $ 1.08 billion, down 6.83 percent. The EDB linked the cumulative fall partly to the weaker Middle Eastern markets, where the tea export earnings contracted 34.22 percent. The shipments to the United Arab Emirates, Iran and Iraq recorded steep declines, although Turkey delivered a substantial growth. The electrical and electronic components were among the strongest performers, with the September earnings surging 88.35 percent to US $ 68.54 million, driven mainly by the insulated wires and cables. The nine-month exports rose 61.05 percent to US $ 508.86 million. The spices, essential oils and oleoresins generated US $ 74.73 million in September, up 73.19 percent, with the pepper earnings jumping 165.38 percent and cinnamon rising 68.27 percent. The cumulative sector earnings increased 30.53 percent to US $ 430.53 million. The rubber and rubber-based products earned US $ 99.31 million during September, up 33.68 percent, supported by stronger tyre and glove exports. The nine-month earnings grew 8.44 percent to US $ 773.88 million. The food and beverage exports rose 27.92 percent in September to US $ 63.77 million, taking the cumulative earnings to US $ 526.31 million, up 20.9 percent. The coconut-based products presented a mixed picture. The September earnings fell 8.88 percent to US $ 111.60 million as the kernel products weakened, despite a 43.52 percent increase in the activated carbon exports. The nine-month coconut product earnings remained 3.68 percent higher at US $ 942.5 million. Among the markets, the United States retained its position as Sri Lanka’s largest single export destination. The September shipments increased 18.06 percent to US $ 281.84 million, although the cumulative earnings were virtually flat at US $ 2.25 billion. India ranked second, ahead of the United Kingdom, with the nine-month exports growing 12.3 percent to US $ 889.84 million. The exports to the United Kingdom declined 9.33 percent to US $ 654.36 million, while the shipments to the EU edged down 0.15 percent. Wijesinghe said the focus must now be on sustaining the growth and widening the export base. “Enhancing value addition, promoting innovation and technology adoption, diversifying the export markets and integrating more deeply into the global value chains will be essential to expanding the export earnings and generating greater economic value for the country,” he said. Sri Lanka’s National Export Development Plan 2026-2030 targets annual export earnings of US $ 36 billion by 2030.

audit.headline: Brazilian President Lula Responds to President Anura’s Congratulatory Note
audit.summary: COLOMBO — Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has responded to the congratulatory message extended by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake following his electoral victory. Posting on his official X (formerly Twitter) account, President Lula recalled his warm meeting with President Dissanayake in India earlier this year in February. Reflecting on his historic election win, the Brazilian President noted that the victory of the Brazilian people demonstrated how democracy can effectively stand against misinformation and extremism, describing it as a landmark achievement. President Lula further expressed Brazil’s commitment to enhancing technical cooperation and strengthening bilateral trade relations between Sri Lanka and Brazil during his new term.

audit.headline: Namal Rajapaksa To Be Held in Custody Until October 29, Over Airbus Bribery Case
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st): Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court today ordered that MP Namal Rajapaksa be held in custody until October 29, in connection with the alleged acceptance of a Rs. 100 million bribe linked to the Airbus aircraft procurement deal. He was produced before the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court today in a case filed by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC). Namal Rajapaksa, who had been in remand custody, was brought to court by prison officials this morning. During the proceedings, Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara, appearing on behalf of the Attorney General, informed the court that the Chief Justice had approved the appointment of a permanent three-judge High Court bench to hear the case against Rajapaksa over the alleged bribery in the Airbus deal.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st): Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court today ordered that MP Namal Rajapaksa be held in custody until October 29, in connection with the alleged acceptance of a Rs. 100 million bribe linked to the Airbus aircraft procurement deal. He was produced before the Colombo Chief Magistrate’s Court today in a case filed by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC). Namal Rajapaksa, who had been in remand custody, was brought to court by prison officials this morning. During the proceedings, Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara, appearing on behalf of the Attorney General, informed the court that the Chief Justice had approved the appointment of a permanent three-judge High Court bench to hear the case against Rajapaksa over the alleged bribery in the Airbus deal. The Deputy Solicitor General also informed the court that indictments had been filed against Rajapaksa before the permanent three-judge High Court. After considering the submissions, the Chief Magistrate ordered that Namal Rajapaksa be produced before the permanent three-judge High Court tomorrow and remain in custody until Thursday.

audit.headline: Sri Lanka’s Bowlers Bundle Pakistan Out For 110
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st): Sri Lanka’s bowlers delivered a dominant performance to dismiss Pakistan for just 110 runs in the fifth match of the tri-nation series featuring Sri Lanka, Pakistan and England. Dilshan Madushanka spearheaded the attack with an outstanding five-wicket haul, conceding just 34 runs. Sahan Arachchige claimed two wickets for 24 runs, while Asitha Fernando, Eshan Malinga and Dunith Wellalage picked up one wicket each. Babar Azam was Pakistan’s top scorer with 29 runs, followed by Hasan Nawaz with 17 and Shaheen Shah Afridi with 15. With Pakistan dismissed for 110, Sri Lanka need just 111 runs in 50 overs to seal victory, putting themselves in a strong position after an impressive bowling display.

audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); The Port of Colombo is preparing for its next big leap, with the United States positioning itself at the heart of an ambitious modernization effort aimed at making one of South Asia's busiest maritime hubs faster, smarter and more competitive. Addressing a regional workshop on Maritime Single Window and Port Community Systems in Colombo, U.S. Ambassador to Sri Lanka Eric Meyer described the Port of Colombo as a vital gateway in global trade, connecting American businesses to markets across South Asia and beyond. According to the Ambassador, what happens at Colombo's waterfront has consequences far beyond Sri Lanka's shores. "What happens in the Port of Colombo matters to American manufacturers, exporters, and consumers who depend on reliable supply chains. That's why I recently announced $17 million in U.S. assistance to modernize the Port of Colombo, bringing American technology and expertise to establish a maritime single window and port community system." The announcement comes as Colombo continues to strengthen its role as a key Indian Ocean logistics hub, handling significant volumes of international cargo. Ambassador Meyer said the goal of the initiative is to build the digital backbone required for a modern port ecosystem, linking ships, customs authorities, government agencies, terminal operators and businesses through a seamless flow of information. "You understand the time and money involved in moving cargo. Our goal is to help Sri Lanka build the digital backbone of a modern port, connecting ships, customs, and other government entities, port operators, and businesses so information can move faster, delays shrink, and costs fall." He noted that speed and efficiency are becoming decisive factors in global commerce, where faster processing directly translates into lower costs and stronger competitiveness. Quoting U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy, Ambassador Meyer stressed that time remains one of the most valuable commodities in global shipping. "When it comes to supply chains, time is money. Faster cargo clearances, vessel registrations, and crew changes mean ships spend less time in port and goods reach their destinations sooner. Last year alone, more than a half a million containers carrying U.S. imports and exports moved through the Port of Colombo." Describing those figures as impressive, the Ambassador said every operational improvement at Colombo benefits both Sri Lankan and American businesses that rely on international trade networks. However, he emphasized that technology alone cannot transform a port. "Success requires cooperation among port authorities, government agencies, shipping lines, terminal operators, and logistics companies. Each of you here in this room has an important role in making these systems work." The workshop also brought together more than a dozen American technology companies, including Calaris and Verix Imaging, showcasing solutions designed to improve efficiency, strengthen cybersecurity and protect sensitive data while ensuring the smooth movement of global trade. "These companies represent the best of American ingenuity and innovation. They bring trusted American technology and expertise that can help ports operate more efficiently, strengthen cybersecurity, protect sensitive data, and keep global trade moving securely." Ambassador Meyer said the event offers regional delegates direct access to American technologies tailored to the changing needs of ports and maritime economies, while opening new opportunities for business partnerships. "The United States, and I think this is very clear, we want to be the partner of choice for countries seeking trusted, innovative technology that delivers results." Positioning Sri Lanka at the centre of a rapidly evolving maritime landscape, the Ambassador noted that the island has historically served as a crossroads of Indian Ocean commerce and is now poised to enter a new era of port operations. "Sri Lanka has long stood at the crossroads of Indian Ocean commerce. With American technology and expertise, we can help write the next chapter of that story, one where goods reach businesses and families faster, shipping costs fall, and the products people depend on arrive when they need them." Calling it a pivotal moment for Colombo and other ports across the region, Ambassador Meyer said the modernization drive has the potential to reshape how cargo moves through Sri Lanka, reducing delays, increasing efficiency and strengthening the country's position in global supply chains.

audit.headline: Schools to Reopen Tomorrow; O/L Practical Exams Postponed in Flood-Hit Areas
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st): Deputy Minister of Education Dr. Madhura Seneviratne says all schools across the island will resume normal operations tomorrow, except for examination centres affected by adverse weather conditions. Schools islandwide were closed today due to severe weather. The Deputy Minister said flooding has been reported in the Sabaragamuwa region, particularly in the Ratnapura District, along with other weather-related disruptions. He added that discussions have been held with the relevant officials at G.C.E. Ordinary Level practical examination centres to postpone examinations where necessary, ensuring that no student is disadvantaged by the prevailing conditions. All other schools are scheduled to resume normal academic activities tomorrow.

audit.headline: Open Warrant Issued for Basil Rajapaksa Over Brown’s Hill Land Case
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st): The Matara Magistrate’s Court issued an open warrant for the arrest of former Minister Basil Rajapaksa. The warrant was issued in connection with a money laundering case filed over a land in Brown’s Hill, Matara. Matara Magistrate Chathura Dissanayake issued the order after considering a request made by the Police Financial Crimes Investigation Division (FCID). The case relates to the alleged purchase of a property in Brown’s Hill, Matara using money obtained through unlawful means. The case has been filed against former Minister Basil Rajapaksa, Ayoma Galappaththi, the sister of his wife, her husband Tissa Galappaththi, and Muditha Jayakody.

audit.headline: 'No One Is Above the Law' - Minister Vows Action Over Custody Death
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); The death of a 29-year-old suspect while in police custody has triggered a high-level investigation, with authorities moving swiftly to suspend three police officers and hand the probe to a specialized criminal investigation unit. Police said investigations into the custodial death have now been assigned to the Western Province South Crimes Division. The development comes after the post-mortem examination into the suspect's death returned an open verdict, leaving investigators to determine exactly what led to the man's death. Amid mounting scrutiny, action was taken yesterday (26) to interdict three officers attached to the Homagama Police Station. Those suspended include two Sub-Inspectors who served as Officers-in-Charge of the Crime Division and the Anti-Vice Raids Unit, as well as a Police Constable who had been on duty at the time of the incident.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); The death of a 29-year-old suspect while in police custody has triggered a high-level investigation, with authorities moving swiftly to suspend three police officers and hand the probe to a specialized criminal investigation unit. Police said investigations into the custodial death have now been assigned to the Western Province South Crimes Division. The development comes after the post-mortem examination into the suspect's death returned an open verdict, leaving investigators to determine exactly what led to the man's death. Amid mounting scrutiny, action was taken yesterday (26) to interdict three officers attached to the Homagama Police Station. Those suspended include two Sub-Inspectors who served as Officers-in-Charge of the Crime Division and the Anti-Vice Raids Unit, as well as a Police Constable who had been on duty at the time of the incident. According to police, the 29-year-old man had been arrested by Homagama Police in connection with narcotics-related offences. He was later admitted to the Homagama Base Hospital after developing a sudden illness and subsequently died while receiving treatment. The incident has once again placed the spotlight on police accountability and the handling of suspects in custody. Commenting on the matter, Minister of Public Security Ananda Wijepala said the Government would ensure an independent and systematic investigation and take action based on its findings. "An independent and proper investigation will be conducted into this incident, and further action will be taken based on the findings of that investigation. Whenever such incidents are reported, we act immediately. The Police, too, must operate within the framework of the law. No officer has the authority to act outside it." The Minister noted that disciplinary action against officers who violate the law has continued in recent years. "1,200 officers have been suspended over the past two years. Therefore, we are prepared to take firm action against decisions and actions that violate the law. The Police do not have the authority to exercise power arbitrarily." In one of his strongest remarks on the issue, the Minister stressed that authorities would not attempt to suppress incidents once they are reported. "When an incident is reported, unlike in the past, we do not attempt to cover it up. We are committed to investigating every incident and ensuring justice is served."

audit.headline: Millions in Compensation for Negombo Prison Clash Victims
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); The Cabinet has approved a compensation and relief package for prison officers who were killed or injured during the clash at the Negombo Prison. Under the approved scheme, the families of each prison officer who lost their life in the incident will receive compensation of Rs. 5 million. Cabinet approval has also been granted to provide Rs. 5 million in compensation to any officer who suffered permanent total disability as a result of the incident. In addition, officers who have been classified as partially disabled with a 100 percent loss of earning capacity will be entitled to compensation amounting to Rs. 4 million. Meanwhile, officers who sustained temporary partial disabilities will receive compensation of Rs. 3 million under the approved relief package.

audit.headline: Madushanka Wrecks Pakistan, Kamindu Finishes the Job

The match belonged to Sri Lanka from the moment their bowlers found their rhythm. After electing to field first, the Lankan attack ripped through Pakistan's batting line-up, exposing the hosts' struggles against disciplined pace and relentless pressure. Pakistan never recovered from the early setbacks, losing wickets at regular intervals as Sri Lanka tightened their grip on the contest. While Babar Azam attempted to steady the innings with 29 runs, no Pakistani batter was able to build a meaningful partnership.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka produced a fierce all-round performance to register a commanding victory over Pakistan in their ODI Tri-Series clash in Lahore, with the visitors completely overpowering the hosts after bowling them out for a paltry 110. The match belonged to Sri Lanka from the moment their bowlers found their rhythm. After electing to field first, the Lankan attack ripped through Pakistan's batting line-up, exposing the hosts' struggles against disciplined pace and relentless pressure. Pakistan never recovered from the early setbacks, losing wickets at regular intervals as Sri Lanka tightened their grip on the contest. While Babar Azam attempted to steady the innings with 29 runs, no Pakistani batter was able to build a meaningful partnership. Once Babar departed, the collapse accelerated, with the home side crashing from 61 for 4 to eventually be dismissed for just 110 in 25.3 overs. The architect of Pakistan's downfall was Dilshan Madushanka. Madushank was outstanding, claiming five wickets and tearing through both the middle and lower order. His aggressive pace, sharp bounce and accurate execution left Pakistan with no answers as he finished with superb figures of 5 for 34. He was supported brilliantly by Sahan Arachchige, who grabbed two wickets, while Asitha Fernando, Eshan Malinga and Dunith Wellalage chipped in with one wicket each to complete a clinical bowling display. Chasing just 111 for victory, Sri Lanka approached the task with complete confidence. Opener Kamindu Mendis anchored the chase superbly with an unbeaten 62, combining composure with authority as the visitors steadily closed in on the target. Pavan Rathnayake provided valuable support with an unbeaten 23 as the pair guided Sri Lanka home without any late drama. Sri Lanka eventually reached 114 for 2 in just 18.1 overs, sealing an eight-wicket victory and underlining their growing momentum in the tournament.

audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka's ambition to become a leading maritime and logistics hub in the Indian Ocean will depend not only on expanding terminals and infrastructure, but also on embracing cutting-edge digital technology, according to Deputy Minister of Ports and Civil Aviation Janitha Ruwan Kodithuwakku. Addressing a regional workshop on maritime digitalization, the Deputy Minister said Sri Lanka's growing role in global and regional supply chains requires a parallel investment in advanced technology to ensure the country remains competitive in an increasingly digital maritime industry. "Sri Lanka's continued development as a maritime logistics hub requires us to strengthen our technological capabilities alongside our physical infrastructure. As we expand port capacity and enhance our role in regional and global supply chains, the adoption of advanced technologies is essential to maximizing the benefits of these investments and responding effectively to the evolving demands of international trade." He noted that modern ports can no longer depend solely on larger terminals and improved physical facilities. Instead, success increasingly depends on efficient information management, streamlined regulatory procedures and seamless coordination among the many stakeholders involved in maritime operations. "Modern ports require more than expanded terminals and improved physical facilities. They also depend on efficient information management, streamlined regulatory procedures and effective coordination among the many stakeholders involved in maritime operations." Kodithuwakku highlighted the importance of the Maritime Single Window and Port Community System, describing them as essential tools for modernizing Sri Lanka's ports. A Maritime Single Window allows ships and their agents to submit required information electronically through a single entry point, significantly reducing bureaucracy and simplifying regulatory processes. Meanwhile, a Port Community System enables real-time information sharing among stakeholders across the port ecosystem, reducing delays, lowering costs and improving operational efficiency. "Together, these digital solutions can enhance operational efficiency, strengthen competitiveness and contribute to a more efficient and reliable maritime transport system."

audit.headline: Sri Lanka’s Tax Burden May Ease; But Only After Revenue Reaches a Safer Level
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka will not reduce its high indirect taxes immediately, Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Anil Jayantha Fernando has said, arguing that the country must first secure stronger revenue mobilisation before it can “reset” a tax structure he acknowledged is burdensome. Fernando said the government remains committed to fiscal consolidation, but signalled that tax relief, including a possible reduction in the 18% Value Added Tax (VAT), could become possible once government revenue reaches a more sustainable share of the economy. The Deputy Minister said the original plan was to raise government revenue to 15.4% of GDP by 2030 as part of the effort to move Sri Lanka out of what he described as an “economic abyss.” However, he said the country had already exceeded that benchmark by the end of 2025, reaching 16.7% of GDP.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); Sri Lanka will not reduce its high indirect taxes immediately, Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning Anil Jayantha Fernando has said, arguing that the country must first secure stronger revenue mobilisation before it can “reset” a tax structure he acknowledged is burdensome. Fernando said the government remains committed to fiscal consolidation, but signalled that tax relief, including a possible reduction in the 18% Value Added Tax (VAT), could become possible once government revenue reaches a more sustainable share of the economy. The Deputy Minister said the original plan was to raise government revenue to 15.4% of GDP by 2030 as part of the effort to move Sri Lanka out of what he described as an “economic abyss.” However, he said the country had already exceeded that benchmark by the end of 2025, reaching 16.7% of GDP. “Now, even at the end of 2025, we were able to achieve a target of 16.7%,” Fernando said. He added that, despite budget ceilings now being governed under the Public Financial Management Act, the government has retained a target in the “15 point something” range for the current year, but believes it can meet or exceed it. “However, it is very clear that we can easily reach that particular target or we can surpass this target,” he said. Fernando said the government expects to raise revenue gradually towards around 18% of GDP by 2030. That additional revenue, he argued, would create fiscal space for public investment while allowing the state to reconsider the current tax framework. “So, we can increase our revenue mobilisation gradually. By 2030, we can reach somewhere around 18,” he said. He said that would “create a kind of space for the government to spend money for much required public investments,” before the government could “think of strategies to reset the present tax structure.” Fernando acknowledged concerns over the current tax burden, particularly the 18% VAT rate, as well as corporate income tax, individual income tax and taxes on dollar income. “The present tax structure, there are some issues we understand,” he said. But he was clear that the government cannot reduce indirect taxation at this stage without undermining revenue mobilisation. “But, at this particular moment, we can't bring it down without damaging this revenue mobilisation,” he said, adding that a reduction would only become possible once the higher revenue level is reached. He said any future changes would be guided by the basic principles of taxation: fairness, simplicity and convenience. Looking ahead to next year’s budget, Fernando said the central challenge would be allocating sufficient funds to create a more conducive environment for economic activity. He identified infrastructure, particularly roads, railways and rural connectivity, as priorities, along with logistics arrangements. “At the same time, some money for social spending as well,” he said. The remarks suggest the government is attempting to balance two competing demands: sustaining the revenue gains needed for fiscal stability, while responding to public pressure over the cost of living and the weight of indirect taxation.

audit.headline: 24 Charges Filed, 59 Witnesses To Testify In Airbus Case Against Namal
audit.summary: COLOMBO (News 1st); The Attorney General informed the Colombo Chief Magistrate's Court that the Chief Justice has appointed a Special Permanent Trial-at-Bar to hear the case against Namal Rajapaksa, National Organiser of the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP), in connection with allegations that he accepted a bribe of Rs. 100 million linked to the Airbus Scandal. Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara, appearing on behalf of the Attorney General, told court that indictments had been filed before the Colombo Permanent Trial-at-Bar under 24 charges. MP Namal Rajapaksa, who remains in remand custody, was once again produced before Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama.
audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); The Attorney General informed the Colombo Chief Magistrate's Court that the Chief Justice has appointed a Special Permanent Trial-at-Bar to hear the case against Namal Rajapaksa, National Organiser of the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP), in connection with allegations that he accepted a bribe of Rs. 100 million linked to the Airbus Scandal. Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara, appearing on behalf of the Attorney General, told court that indictments had been filed before the Colombo Permanent Trial-at-Bar under 24 charges. MP Namal Rajapaksa, who remains in remand custody, was once again produced before Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama. During proceedings, Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara informed court that, as indictments have already been filed before the Permanent Trial-at-Bar, this would be the final occasion on which the matter would be called before the Magistrate's Court. The Deputy Solicitor General further stated that 59 witnesses are expected to be called to testify during the hearing of the 24 charges. President's Counsel Shavindra Fernando and Ali Sabry, appearing on behalf of Namal Rajapaksa, requested that their client be granted bail under any conditions deemed appropriate by the court. Here's a translated extract of the submission made by President's Counsel Ali Sabry: "The Constitution clearly states that every accused person is presumed innocent until proven guilty. We are prepared to appear before the High Court on any date directed by court. On that day, the High Court may decide whether to grant bail or remand the accused. However, that issue is not relevant today. This court has the authority to grant bail to the suspect at this stage. Therefore, we respectfully request that bail be granted under any conditions the court may impose." Responding to the application, Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara argued that the Magistrate's Court no longer has the authority to grant bail since indictments have already been filed before the High Court, and requested that the suspect remain in remand custody until summons are issued by the Trial-at-Bar. Here's a translated extract of the submission made by President's Counsel Shavindra Fernando: "Your Honour, I agree with my learned friend. Jurisdiction over this matter now rests with the Trial-at-Bar because indictments have already been filed. Once the indictments are filed, any orders previously issued by this court in relation to this case effectively come to an end. The authority to determine whether bail should be granted now lies with the High Court. Therefore, I respectfully request that these proceedings before this court be concluded without issuing any further orders affecting this matter." After considering the submissions made by both parties, Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama ordered that the suspect remain in detention until October 29, pending his production before the Trial-at-Bar. Here's a translated extract of the statement made by Colombo Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama: "This court does not have the authority to grant bail at this stage. The only order I am able to make at present is to direct that the suspect be produced before the Permanent Trial-at-Bar where the indictments have been filed as soon as possible. Accordingly, the suspect should be produced before the Permanent Trial-at-Bar on the 28th. Thereafter, the court is to be informed of the progress on the 30th. Until the suspect is produced before the Permanent Trial-at-Bar, I order that he be held in prison custody until the 29th."

audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); The Port of Colombo already ranks among the world's leading container hubs, handling billions of dollars in trade each year. But according to Sri Lanka Ports Authority Chairman Dr. Parakrama Dissanayake, the port's next leap forward will not be driven by more cranes, bigger yards or additional manpower. It will be driven by intelligence, connectivity and digital transformation. Addressing a workshop on Maritime Single Window and Port Community Systems, Dr. Dissanayake painted a picture of a global shipping industry under immense pressure, with congestion and supply chain disruptions continuing to challenge major ports around the world. "Globally, as we all know, supply chains have been disrupted, facing enormous challenges on ports. On any given day, 4.2 million TEUs are awaiting a berth." While Colombo is performing better than many ports internationally, he noted that between 10,000 and 12,000 TEUs are still waiting for berthing opportunities outside the Port of Colombo on a daily basis. Highlighting the scale of operations, Dr. Dissanayake said the Port of Colombo is expected to handle approximately nine million TEUs in 2026, maintaining its status among the world's top 20 container ports. Yet, perhaps the most striking figure was the port's contribution to international commerce. "The Port of Colombo's contribution towards global and regional trade through transshipment is approximately US$250 billion. I repeat that figure. It's approximately US$250 billion." In addition, Colombo facilitates approximately US$30 billion worth of Sri Lanka's merchandise trade, stressing on its central role in both the national economy and regional supply chains. Traditionally, ports have expanded capacity by constructing additional berths, increasing yard space, investing in machinery and hiring more personnel. However, Dr. Dissanayake argued that the future lies elsewhere. "We hardly speak of increasing port capacity through digital platforms like PCS and the Maritime Single Window." According to studies cited by the SLPA Chairman, reducing container dwell time from 11 days to five days could increase terminal capacity by an astonishing 118 percent. A further reduction from five days to just 3.3 days could raise yard capacity by another 53 percent. The scale of inefficiencies associated with documentation is equally significant. "Going by IMO data, average time spent on documentation at each port of call was 191 minutes." With approximately 4,100 vessel calls handled annually by the Port of Colombo, the port spends around 13,000 hours every year dealing with paper-based documentation. To illustrate the transformative potential of digital systems, Dr. Dissanayake pointed to a competing port in West Asia that implemented a Port Community System and Maritime Single Window. "By implementing a PCS and MSW, a competing port in West Asia was able to eliminate 42 million paper document exchanges and 12.7 million port visits." He also cited a developed-country port that reported annual logistics savings of US$270 million through similar digital initiatives, compared with the US$17 million investment currently being directed toward modernising Colombo's operations. For Colombo, the expected benefits are substantial. Faster vessel turnaround times, stronger transshipment reliability, improved container dwell times and lower operating costs for shipping lines could significantly enhance the port's competitiveness. "By coming up with this system, we can reduce operating costs for our clients and for our shipping lines." Dr. Dissanayake also expressed appreciation to the United States Government for its support toward the modernisation initiative, describing it as an important opportunity for Sri Lanka's port sector. "Ports of yesterday competed on infrastructure. Ports of today compete on efficiency. Ports of tomorrow will compete on intelligence and connectivity."

audit.body: COLOMBO (News 1st); A motion filed by President's Counsel Ali Sabry, seeking bail for Namal Rajapaksa on what he described as exceptional grounds in the Krrish case, in which allegations have been made regarding the acceptance of a Rs. 70 million bribe, was taken up before the Colombo Chief Magistrate's Court. During submissions, President's Counsel Ali Sabry informed court that the suspect's father, former President Mahinda Rajapaksa, and mother, Shiranthi Rajapaksa, are currently facing serious health challenges. Here's a translated extract of the submission made by President's Counsel Ali Sabry: "The suspect's father is currently suffering from recurring high blood pressure and depression and has been hospitalized for treatment before returning home. However, he now requires care and attention. Until now, that responsibility was carried out by the suspect's mother, Shiranthi Rajapaksa. However, she too is currently hospitalized due to a heart condition. The main artery supplying blood to her heart has become blocked. Doctors have identified a risk that the oxygen supply route to the heart could become completely obstructed. She has been advised to undergo an angiogram and two surgical procedures. One of those procedures has already been carried out, and she is presently in hospital with the assistance of a pacemaker. According to medical recommendations, she is scheduled to undergo open-heart surgery as her second operation at 4.00 p.m. today. It is a life-threatening procedure. After today's surgery, it cannot be said with certainty whether the suspect's mother will remain alive. She is no longer in a position to care for Mahinda Rajapaksa, and there is now a situation where she herself requires care. If bail is granted today, the suspect will be able to visit his mother. Today could even be the last day he sees his mother, Your Honour. He is the eldest son of Mahinda Rajapaksa and Shiranthi Rajapaksa. They lived in the same household. Remanding a suspect should not operate as a punishment." Appearing on behalf of the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption, Assistant Director Legal Thanuja Bandara stated that she had not been informed of the motion beforehand. She further told court that she became aware of the application only after arriving at court for another matter. Here's a translated extract of the submission made by CIABOC Assistant Director of Legal Thanuja Bandara: "The complainant requires time to make lengthy written submissions in response to the facts presented today on behalf of the suspect. Under the Anti-Corruption Act, and based on the certificate submitted by the Director General of the Bribery Commission, the suspect must remain in remand custody until investigations are completed. Bail cannot be granted unless exceptional circumstances are established. The certificate submitted against the suspect under Section 149 of the Anti-Corruption Act cannot be challenged." Responding to those submissions, President's Counsel Ali Sabry argued that the matters presented before court constituted the exceptional circumstances required for bail. Here's a translated extract of the submission made by President's Counsel Ali Sabry: "Your Honour, we have not challenged the certificate submitted under Section 149 of the Anti-Corruption Act today. We made no submissions on that issue. We will challenge it at the appropriate stage if necessary. The matters placed before court today relate solely to the exceptional circumstances that have now arisen in support of the suspect's bail application." After considering the submissions made by both parties, the Magistrate directed the complainant to inform court tomorrow of its position regarding the suspect's bail application. Here's a translated extract of the statement made by Asanga S. Bodaragama, the Colombo Chief Magistrate: "A lengthy bail application had previously been filed on behalf of the suspect. However, the matters raised today were not included in that application. Therefore, this court has the authority to determine whether these facts amount to exceptional circumstances warranting bail. Nevertheless, it is necessary to hear the complainant's position on this matter as well. Accordingly, the complainant must inform court of its position tomorrow, after which I will make an appropriate order regarding the bail application." The motion is scheduled to be taken up again tomorrow. In relation to the same case, Namal Rajapaksa and former Krrish Company Director Janaki Siriwardena remain in remand custody until November 6.

audit.headline: BASL calls for independent probe into Police custodial death
audit.summary: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has expressed grave concern over the death of a 29-year-old suspect in the custody of the Homagama Police, calling for an immediate, impartial and transparent investigation. In a statement, the BASL identified the deceased as Ishara Harshakumara, a father of two from Kiriwaththuduwa, who had been arrested in connection with a drug-related investigation. Family members who visited the Homagama Police Station on 25 October, 2026 reported observing physical injuries on the suspect, which they believed indicated that he had been severely assaulted, the BASL said. The Police Spokesman, however, gave a different account, stating that the suspect had developed a sudden illness during an operation and died following admission to hospital.
audit.body: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) has expressed grave concern over the death of a 29-year-old suspect in the custody of the Homagama Police, calling for an immediate, impartial and transparent investigation. In a statement, the BASL identified the deceased as Ishara Harshakumara, a father of two from Kiriwaththuduwa, who had been arrested in connection with a drug-related investigation. Family members who visited the Homagama Police Station on 25 October, 2026 reported observing physical injuries on the suspect, which they believed indicated that he had been severely assaulted, the BASL said. The Police Spokesman, however, gave a different account, stating that the suspect had developed a sudden illness during an operation and died following admission to hospital. Citing these conflicting accounts, the BASL stressed the need for a credible and independent investigation to establish the circumstances of the death. It said the State has a fundamental responsibility to protect the lives, health and physical safety of individuals in police custody, and that any allegation of custodial violence or ill-treatment must be treated seriously. If wrongdoing is established, those responsible must be held accountable under the law, it added. The Homagama Magistrate’s Court has ordered a post-mortem examination, and a preliminary inquiry has commenced under the direction of the Homagama Assistant Superintendent of Police, the BASL noted. It called on the Inspector General of Police (IGP) and relevant authorities to ensure that all evidence is properly preserved and examined, and that investigations are conducted without interference or prejudice. The BASL said it would consider further action if necessary and keep its members and the public informed of developments.

audit.headline: Cabinet clears $ 60 m OPEC Fund Loan
audit.summary: Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa - For Mahaweli Water Security Investment Program Phase II The Cabinet of Ministers has approved entering into an agreement with the OPEC Fund for International Development (OFID) to obtain a $ 60 million loan facility for Phase II of the Mahaweli Water Security Investment Program. Following negotiations, the OPEC Fund agreed to provide the facility in two components of $ 48 million and $ 12 million. The Cabinet had earlier approved negotiations for the loan on 20 July 2026, as part of the proposed co-financing arrangement. The Phase II of the program is aimed at achieving the Government’s long-term objectives of enhancing food security, strengthening water resources management, improving resilience to climate change and reducing poverty in dry zone areas.
audit.body: Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa - For Mahaweli Water Security Investment Program Phase II The Cabinet of Ministers has approved entering into an agreement with the OPEC Fund for International Development (OFID) to obtain a $ 60 million loan facility for Phase II of the Mahaweli Water Security Investment Program. Following negotiations, the OPEC Fund agreed to provide the facility in two components of $ 48 million and $ 12 million. The Cabinet had earlier approved negotiations for the loan on 20 July 2026, as part of the proposed co-financing arrangement. The Phase II of the program is aimed at achieving the Government’s long-term objectives of enhancing food security, strengthening water resources management, improving resilience to climate change and reducing poverty in dry zone areas. “The estimated total cost is $ 536.5 million, with funding to be raised through a multi-development partnership approach,” Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said at the weekly post-Cabinet meeting media briefing yesterday. The Asian Development Bank has already agreed to provide $ 200 million. He said under this phase, the remaining section of the main tunnel will be completed, including excavation of around 7 kilometers and related finishing works. Open and covered canals, waterways and small tunnel sections totaling about 68 kilometers will also be constructed, along with an 8-kilometer section of the Allapokana Irrigation Project canal. The phase also includes the development of commercial agricultural infrastructure, comprising about 13 pressure distribution networks to reliably and efficiently supply irrigation water to high-value crops and field crops. In addition, he said the agricultural production systems will be transformed through the introduction of climate-resilient value chains and expanded access to financial services and agricultural project services for farmers. The proposal to this effect was submitted by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in his capacity as the Finance, Planning and Economic Development Minister.

audit.body: The Sri Lanka Export Development Board (EDB) has held a series of export-oriented business clinics in the North Western Province, attracting more than 100 participants across the Kurunegala and Puttalam districts. The clinics, held on 11 September in Kurunegala and on 16 October in Puttalam, were organised by the EDB’s North Western Provincial Office together with District and Divisional Secretariat Offices. They targeted export-oriented SMEs in sectors including coconut and coconut-based products, spices, food and beverages, ornamental fish, cut flowers and foliage, textiles and apparel, and handicrafts. Export Development Officers (EDOs) stationed in District and Divisional Secretariat Offices in both districts supported the program. The program aimed to bridge the knowledge gap among regional SMEs. It offered tailored advice on export-related challenges, raised awareness of export procedures and requirements, and sought to strengthen participants’ business capabilities and export readiness. Kurunegala District Secretary D.M.K.C. Dissanayake and Kurunegala Additional District Secretary (Lands) Niluka K. Jayawardhana attended the Kurunegala program, while the Puttalam program was organised with the Chilaw Divisional Secretariat Office. Officials from the Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Industrial Development Board (IDB), Small Enterprise Development Division (SEDD), National Enterprise Development Authority (NEDA) and financial institutions held one-on-one advisory sessions with entrepreneurs. The sessions addressed specific product and business development needs and provided information on available support services. Entrepreneurs were also able to connect with providers of export-quality packaging and labelling, logistics, certification, and testing and inspection services. Participant feedback indicated a high level of satisfaction with the arrangements, the EDB said. The EDB plans follow-up activities with participants to identify their specific needs, assess areas requiring further assistance and facilitate appropriate support. The aim is to ensure continuity of support beyond the clinics and ultimately increase the contribution of regional enterprises to national exports.

audit.headline: Fairway Holdings appoints Ashean Karthelis as Group Managing Director
audit.summary: Ashean Karthelis Fairway Holdings Ltd., yesterday said it has appointed Ashean Karthelis as Group Managing Director, marking an important milestone in the group’s continuing journey of growth. The appointment recognises Ashean’s contribution over the past four and a half years in bringing greater structure, stability and strategic direction to Fairway’s diverse business portfolio. Having served as Group Chief Executive Officer, he has helped strengthen organisational alignment, accountability and coordination across the Group, establishing a foundation for its next phase of development.
audit.body: Ashean Karthelis Fairway Holdings Ltd., yesterday said it has appointed Ashean Karthelis as Group Managing Director, marking an important milestone in the group’s continuing journey of growth. The appointment recognises Ashean’s contribution over the past four and a half years in bringing greater structure, stability and strategic direction to Fairway’s diverse business portfolio. Having served as Group Chief Executive Officer, he has helped strengthen organisational alignment, accountability and coordination across the Group, establishing a foundation for its next phase of development. As Group Managing Director, Ashean will continue to provide overall Group leadership across real estate, leisure, construction and interior solutions, renewable energy and other business interests, with an increased focus on driving growth, strengthening business performance and ensuring long-term sustainability. Chairman Virath de Alwis said: “Ashean’s appointment as Group Managing Director is a recognition of the contribution he has made to Fairway over the past four and a half years. His commitment to bringing structure and stability across our businesses has helped strengthen the Group’s foundations and prepare us for the opportunities ahead. “Having worked closely with Ashean from the beginning of his journey at Fairway, we have developed a shared understanding of our future aspirations and the responsibility we carry in building on our Founder’s legacy. I look forward to continuing this partnership as we take Fairway to new heights, with a clear focus on growth, sustainability and our vision of Creating Vibrant Communities.” A defining influence on Ashean’s leadership journey at Fairway was the two and a half years he spent working under the guidance and mentorship of the late Founder Chairman, Hemaka de Alwis. This experience gave him a deeply rooted understanding of Fairway’s ethos, its entrepreneurial spirit and the Founder’s belief in creating businesses that contribute meaningfully to people’s lives and communities. His close working relationship with Virath de Alwis, established from the outset of his tenure, has complemented that grounding with a shared appreciation of the next generation’s ambitions for Fairway. Together, these relationships provide continuity between the Group’s founding values and its future direction under Virath’s chairmanship. Director Sundari de Alwis said: “Hemaka built Fairway with a vision that extended beyond individual businesses. He believed in creating vibrant communities and in the people who would help bring that vision to life. The time Ashean spent under his guidance gave him a valuable understanding of those beliefs and the values at the heart of Fairway. “It is encouraging to see that understanding reflected in Ashean’s commitment to the Group and in the close working relationship he has built with Virath. This appointment recognises his contribution and the confidence we place in him to help carry Fairway’s legacy forward while supporting its continued growth.” The appointment reinforces Fairway Holdings’ commitment to leadership continuity, disciplined execution and sustainable expansion. Working closely with the Chairman, Board of Directors and business leadership teams, Ashean will lead the translation of the Group’s ambitions into clear priorities and measurable outcomes across its business verticals.

audit.headline: Govt. signals stronger capital market push in 2027 Budget
audit.summary: Finance and Planning Deputy Minister Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando – Pic by Sameera Wijesingha - Deputy Finance Minister says Govt. considering tax structure reset; indirect tax cuts possible once revenue goals met - New SOE Act to let State firms be incorporated as autonomous companies; Govt. to exit trading, hotels - Most of SEC’s 12 capital market development proposals accepted, some to feature in 12 Nov.
