audit.body: Finance and Planning Deputy Minister Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando – Pic by Sameera Wijesingha - Deputy Finance Minister says Govt. considering tax structure reset; indirect tax cuts possible once revenue goals met - New SOE Act to let State firms be incorporated as autonomous companies; Govt. to exit trading, hotels - Most of SEC’s 12 capital market development proposals accepted, some to feature in 12 Nov. Budget - Rs. 2 t earmarked for capital expenditure as Govt. seeks shift from stabilisation to transformation Finance and Planning Deputy Minister Dr. Anil Jayantha Fernando yesterday said the Government’s capital market policies would be far more visible in the 2027 Budget, conceding that steps taken over the past two years had not been widely seen, leading some to conclude it had done little for the market. “You will see that visibility in a bigger way in this (2027) Budget,” Dr. Fernando told the Institutional Investor Forum, ‘From Resilience to Sustainable Growth – Industry Forum 2026’, hosted by the Securities and Exchange Commission of Sri Lanka (SEC) and the Colombo Stock Exchange (CSE). The Budget proposals will be presented on 12 November, 2026. He said most of the 12 capital market development proposals submitted by the SEC had already been discussed and accepted by the Finance Ministry. Some will be included in the Budget proposals, while the remainder will be discussed further and implemented in consultation with the CSE and the SEC. Dr. Fernando said the Government had achieved most of its macroeconomic stabilisation targets ahead of or within the expected timeframe, earning recognition from local stakeholders, diplomatic missions, international agencies and independent rating agencies. The next task, he said, was to move beyond that phase. “Our challenge is not to live only within stabilisation. We need to move forward from stabilisation to real transformation, where investment is much needed, both local and foreign,” he said. He identified domestic savings as the immediate opportunity, noting a gap between savings and investment in Sri Lanka, and said the capital market had a critical role in pooling scattered savings and channelling money into the real economy. To build an environment conducive to investment, the Government will allocate Rs. 2 trillion for capital expenditure, prioritising roads, railways, rural connectivity and networks, logistics, and some social spending. Dr. Fernando, however, conceded that existing bureaucratic systems and resources constrained the State’s ability to spend at speed, and said discussions on accelerating disbursement were already under way. On fiscal policy, he said revenue mobilisation was well ahead of plan. The original target was to raise Government revenue to 15.4% of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) by 2030, but the country had already exceeded 16% by end-2025. This year’s target, set under ceilings referenced to the Public Financial Management Act, has been kept at around 15%, which he said could easily be reached. Once that level is secured, Dr. Fernando said, the Government would have space to fund much-needed public investment and could then consider strategies to reset the present tax structure. He acknowledged issues in corporate income tax and individual income tax, but said rates could not be brought down at this stage without delaying revenue mobilisation. Once revenue reaches the required level, there is a possibility of reducing indirect taxation as well, he said, adding that all tax policy changes would be guided by the principles of fairness, simplicity and convenience. Turning to State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs), he said only selected entities among the 527 classified as SOEs were engaged in commercial enterprise, with many carrying the label due to legal or other requirements. “The Government is not interested in engaging in ordinary economic activities such as trading or running a hotel. Our main task is to facilitate,” he said. Some SOEs will be diversified and others merged, while certain entities, including utilities such as energy, may be retained, either with private sector collaboration or solely with State investment, to prevent market manipulation. A new SOE Act would allow these entities to be reorganised under one umbrella and incorporated as companies with the autonomy to take decisions based on market conditions and risk. Dr. Fernando cautioned that the process would take time. He also said required legal amendments would be introduced, with new Acts in the pipeline for presentation to Parliament, and that the single window project for investment facilitation through technology was nearing completion. On monetary conditions, Dr. Fernando said interest rates were relatively high but not volatile, following decisions by the Central Bank to address external sector issues. In the long run, he said, inflation and interest rates must come down. He flagged the Middle East crisis as an unquantifiable risk, noting that even global experts could not predict its duration or intensity, alongside the escalating global trade war, natural disasters, El Niño and climate change. Citing the Government’s handling of recent currency pressure as evidence of its commitment to market fundamentals, Dr. Fernando said rumours of bans on motor vehicle and non-essential imports following the Middle East war had fuelled speculation, pushing the import bill up by around $ 2.5 billion a month over three to four months and putting enormous pressure on the currency. The rate prevailing at the time could not be explained by interest rate differentials, he said. “We did not take unnecessary decisions such as pegging the currency or artificially controlling the market. We let the market run, because we had confidence in our foreign exchange inflows,” he said. Applying the same principle to equities, he said market distortions arose when prices deviated from fundamentals, often driven by manipulation and information asymmetry, a situation where some participants hold information, including inside information, that others do not. Such practices had fostered a negative public perception of the market and made savers reluctant to invest. Regulators and stakeholders were now working to uphold fundamentals and a level playing field, he said, adding that the Government would not allow private interests to conflict with the public interest. “We hope that next year, in addition to what we have achieved so far, there will be new developments in the capital market and more foreign investment in the capital market,” Dr. Fernando said. Central Bank Governor Dr. P. Nandalal Weerasinghe, SEC Chairman Senior Prof. D.B.P.H. Dissabandara and CSE Chairman Dimuthu Abeyesekera also addressed the forum and took part in a panel discussion.

audit.headline: IFS Customer Day at University of Moratuwa bridges ERP learning with industry
audit.summary: IFS Customer Day at University of Moratuwa Bridges ERP Learning with Industry SEBSA, in partnership with IFS and the University of Moratuwa, hosted IFS Customer Day at the University of Moratuwa’s Faculty of Business on 30 September. The event brought together IFS customers, industry professionals, lecturers, and students to connect academic learning with real-world ERP applications. The event was part of a long-term Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) project by SEBSA and IFS for the University of Moratuwa’s academic program, Minor (Degree) in ERP Systems. As part of this initiative, SEBSA delivered several modules using IFS Cloud as the practical learning platform, enabling students to gain hands-on experience and develop industry-relevant skills before entering the workforce.
audit.body: IFS Customer Day at University of Moratuwa Bridges ERP Learning with Industry SEBSA, in partnership with IFS and the University of Moratuwa, hosted IFS Customer Day at the University of Moratuwa’s Faculty of Business on 30 September. The event brought together IFS customers, industry professionals, lecturers, and students to connect academic learning with real-world ERP applications. The event was part of a long-term Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) project by SEBSA and IFS for the University of Moratuwa’s academic program, Minor (Degree) in ERP Systems. As part of this initiative, SEBSA delivered several modules using IFS Cloud as the practical learning platform, enabling students to gain hands-on experience and develop industry-relevant skills before entering the workforce. Silvermill Group DGM IT – Information Security Kelum Wickramasinghe and Airport and Aviation Services Sri Lanka Head of Finance Jayalath Abeywardena shared their organisations’ experiences with IFS and discussed how ERP knowledge and technology support real business needs. SEBSA CEO Muthuraja Nanayakkara said the program has delivered IFS ERP education to four batches across 12 semesters over the past two and a half years. More than 160 students have gained knowledge of eight key IFS Cloud modules through over 4,500 learning hours. University of Moratuwa Faculty of Business Senior Lecturer Dr. Indra Mahakalanda said that some graduates face challenges finding internships and employment that align with their field of specialisation and interests. He noted that initiatives such as IFS Customer Day help bridge this gap by giving students industry exposure and enabling them to apply their skills and knowledge in the workplace, creating value for employers. For students, the event provided an opportunity to understand how ERP systems are used in industry, and what employers expect from graduates with Industrial Artificial Intelligence (AI) shaping the future. The event also gave IFS customers an opportunity to connect with students who already have exposure to IFS Cloud. SEBSA Senior Vice President – Growth and Innovation Martin Gunnarsson also highlighted the importance of building the right professional connections, encouraging students to use opportunities such as this to create connections that can support their career growth. IFS Program Manager Minindu Somaratne explained how Industrial AI is transforming traditional asset-intensive industries and how IFS is embedding agentic capabilities into everyday operations through the IFS.ai platform. He also highlighted the importance of developing young talent as the IFS ecosystem continues to grow, noting that future professionals will need the skills to understand, apply, and work with emerging technologies such as Industrial AI. The event highlighted the growing connection between academic education and industry requirements, while strengthening the pipeline of graduates with hands-on experience on IFS Cloud and ERP systems.

audit.headline: PickMe’s growing network drives operating leverage and value for earners and shareholders
audit.summary: - 2Q revenue up 37% to Rs. 2.9 b, platform GTV tops Rs. 28.5 b with Rs. 24.7 b flowing to independent drivers, merchants - 1H GTV up 43% to Rs. 53.8 b, generating Rs. 46.7 b in earnings for independent drivers, merchants Digital Mobility Solutions Lanka PLC, owner and operator of the PickMe platform, yesterday said it posted revenue of Rs. 2.9 billion in the second quarter of FY26/27, up 37% year-on-year, alongside a 37% increase in total platform movements. The platform facilitated Rs. 28.5 billion in Gross Transaction Value (GTV), with Rs. 24.7 billion flowing directly to independent drivers and merchants. Higher transaction volumes and stronger operating leverage lifted net profit by 53% year-on-year to Rs. 784 million. This performance supported the Board’s approval of an interim dividend of Rs. 2.75 per share, representing a 65% payout ratio.
audit.body: - 2Q revenue up 37% to Rs. 2.9 b, platform GTV tops Rs. 28.5 b with Rs. 24.7 b flowing to independent drivers, merchants - 1H GTV up 43% to Rs. 53.8 b, generating Rs. 46.7 b in earnings for independent drivers, merchants Digital Mobility Solutions Lanka PLC, owner and operator of the PickMe platform, yesterday said it posted revenue of Rs. 2.9 billion in the second quarter of FY26/27, up 37% year-on-year, alongside a 37% increase in total platform movements. The platform facilitated Rs. 28.5 billion in Gross Transaction Value (GTV), with Rs. 24.7 billion flowing directly to independent drivers and merchants. Higher transaction volumes and stronger operating leverage lifted net profit by 53% year-on-year to Rs. 784 million. This performance supported the Board’s approval of an interim dividend of Rs. 2.75 per share, representing a 65% payout ratio. In a statement, the Company said the results reflect the operating leverage created by increasing network density. Connecting more consumers, drivers and merchants enables PickMe to improve platform efficiency, deliver greater value for its users and enhance overall earnings by spreading technology and operating costs across a larger volume of activity. PickMe Founder and CEO Jiffry Zulfer said the performance demonstrated the economic potential of digitalisation in the shared economy. “Our business earns a small share of a growing volume of transactions, while the greater share of that value remains with the independent drivers and merchants providing the services. As more consumers, earners and businesses join the platform, greater network density creates more earning opportunities while allowing PickMe to invest in technology that continuously improves user experience and generates strong returns for shareholders. That is the strength of the model; the platform succeeds as the people and businesses using it grow.” PickMe Chairman Ajit Gunewardene said the dividend balanced shareholder returns with the Company’s continuing investment requirements. “The interim dividend reflects the Board’s confidence in PickMe’s performance, financial position and long-term prospects. Our approach is to provide meaningful returns to shareholders while retaining the capacity to invest in technology, strengthen the platform and pursue future growth opportunities. As a locally developed technology business, PickMe also brings more consumers, independent earners and businesses into the digital economy as it grows, helping bridge the digital divide.” Average monthly unique consumers reached 2.1 million during the quarter, increasing 38% year-on-year. Average monthly unique driver earners were up 58% year-on-year. Total platform movements also increased 18% quarter-on-quarter, with growth recorded across all product verticals. The CEO said restoring supply reliability following the first-quarter fuel disruption had been an operational priority. “Our immediate focus was to improve driver availability and maintain a reliable service as demand recovered. The growth in consumer activity, earner participation and platform movements shows that these measures are delivering results. We will continue to focus on service quality, supply reliability and disciplined execution as the platform expands.” For the first half of FY26/27, revenue rose 38% year-on-year to Rs. 5.4 billion from Rs. 3.9 billion in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. Average monthly unique consumers and driver earners both reached all-time highs during the period, while total platform movements increased 39% year-on-year. First-half GTV rose 43% year-on-year to Rs. 53.8 billion from Rs. 37.6 billion, generating Rs. 46.7 billion in earnings for independent drivers and merchants. Higher transaction volumes, operating leverage and continued cost discipline lifted first-half operating profit by 44% to Rs. 1.9 billion from Rs. 1.3 billion a year earlier. Net profit increased 49% to Rs. 1.4 billion from Rs. 950 million, while earnings per share rose to Rs. 4.24 from Rs. 2.85.

audit.headline: Placating demons still
audit.summary: Sri Lanka has spent recent weeks listening to a curse. Vas Kavi, anonymous verses invoking malevolent forces against the country’s rulers, have spread rapidly across social media. The latest calls on Vajrapani, a fearsome form of the deity Sakra, to strike down an unnamed ruler accused of gaining power through falsehoods. The verses followed a campaign by a group of Buddhist monks demanding the release of a fellow monk sentenced to six years’ rigorous imprisonment for contempt of court. During the protest, participants reportedly drove wooden nails into a clay effigy in the name of the demon Maha Sona. It is tempting to treat this as a curiosity, or as proof that a nation proud of its Theravada heritage has strayed from the Buddha’s rational teachings. A former Central Bank Deputy Governor argued as much in these pages this week.
audit.body: Sri Lanka has spent recent weeks listening to a curse. Vas Kavi, anonymous verses invoking malevolent forces against the country’s rulers, have spread rapidly across social media. The latest calls on Vajrapani, a fearsome form of the deity Sakra, to strike down an unnamed ruler accused of gaining power through falsehoods. The verses followed a campaign by a group of Buddhist monks demanding the release of a fellow monk sentenced to six years’ rigorous imprisonment for contempt of court. During the protest, participants reportedly drove wooden nails into a clay effigy in the name of the demon Maha Sona. It is tempting to treat this as a curiosity, or as proof that a nation proud of its Theravada heritage has strayed from the Buddha’s rational teachings. A former Central Bank Deputy Governor argued as much in these pages this week. Yet the more useful explanation may be economic rather than doctrinal. Decades ago, the anthropologists Gananath Obeyesekere and Richard Gombrich set out to explain why sorcery and spirit cults were flourishing in and around Colombo, not in remote villages. Their answer, in Buddhism Transformed, was that the post-independence economy had failed to keep pace with rising expectations. People became poorer and more mobile, and the village community that once cushioned hardship began to disappear. These new stresses created new psychological needs. Gods with fewer moral scruples gained followers, and the sorcery deity Huniyan rose from demon to divinity in urban shrines. Obeyesekere returned to these themes in ‘Placating the Demons’, examining how ideas about demonic misfortune, possession and sorcery persist in new guises. The point is not that Sri Lankans are unusually credulous. It is that people who feel they have little control over their circumstances look for other ways to explain misfortune and seek redress. When institutions appear unresponsive, the curse becomes a form of protest. When the economy offers no clear route upward, the shrine at least promises intervention. Seen this way, the Vas Kavi episode is less a cultural throwback than a symptom. The economic crisis of 2022, when the country exhausted its foreign exchange reserves and could not import basic necessities, left deep scars. Stability has since returned, but stability at the macro level is not the same as recovery for every household. Where gains from the turnaround are unevenly shared, the gap between those who have regained their footing and those still struggling breeds resentment that viral verses can easily tap. That matters for growth. Once the International Monetary Fund (IMF) program ends, Sri Lanka will need sustained growth to consolidate its recovery. Growth depends on broad confidence in institutions, in the rule of law and in the prospect that effort will be rewarded. A society that turns to curses to settle political disputes is signalling that such confidence is thin. The same column rightly noted that pressure to pardon a person convicted of contempt of court sits uneasily with the predictability that serious investors require. Sri Lanka has spent centuries placating demons. The surest way to make them redundant is to give its people fewer reasons to call on them. The answer cannot simply be to urge people to be more rational. Obeyesekere’s work suggests superstition recedes as insecurity does. That points to growth that reaches beyond Colombo’s upper tiers, education that rewards understanding over rote learning, social protection that reaches those still recovering from the crisis, and institutions that citizens trust to hear their grievances without help from Maha Sona.

audit.headline: Secondary Bond market yields increase
audit.summary: - Rs. 100 b T-Bill auction in focus - Rs. 100 b T-Bond auction details announced - Rupee dips marginally By Wealth Trust Securities The secondary Bond market yesterday saw yields increase, mainly on selected tenors on the back of selling interest. Activity was seen at a moderate level while transaction volumes were boosted by the execution of several block transactions as the elevated yield levels attracted absorptive buying interest. In terms of the trade summary, the 15.10.30 traded at the rates of 11.60%-11.63%. On the 2031 maturity bucket, the 01.02.31, 15.03.31 and 01.12.31 maturities traded at the rates of 11.75%, 11.80% and 11.90% respectively. The 01.11.33 maturity traded at the rate of 12.37%. The 2034 tenors moved up with the 15.06.34 and 15.09.34 maturities trading at the rates of 12.50%-12.55% and 12.55%-12.57% respectively.
audit.body: - Rs. 100 b T-Bill auction in focus - Rs. 100 b T-Bond auction details announced - Rupee dips marginally By Wealth Trust Securities The secondary Bond market yesterday saw yields increase, mainly on selected tenors on the back of selling interest. Activity was seen at a moderate level while transaction volumes were boosted by the execution of several block transactions as the elevated yield levels attracted absorptive buying interest. In terms of the trade summary, the 15.10.30 traded at the rates of 11.60%-11.63%. On the 2031 maturity bucket, the 01.02.31, 15.03.31 and 01.12.31 maturities traded at the rates of 11.75%, 11.80% and 11.90% respectively. The 01.11.33 maturity traded at the rate of 12.37%. The 2034 tenors moved up with the 15.06.34 and 15.09.34 maturities trading at the rates of 12.50%-12.55% and 12.55%-12.57% respectively. The Treasury Bill auction scheduled for today will have a total of Rs. 100 billion on offer, comprising of Rs. 50.00 billion on the 91-day maturity, Rs. 25.00 billion on the 182-day maturity and Rs. 25.00 billion on the 364-day maturity. The amount on offer is below the estimated Rs. 130.25 billion in maturities corresponding to the auction. At the weekly Treasury Bill auction conducted last Wednesday (21st Oct), weighted average yields on the 182-day and 364-day tenors remained unchanged at 9.44% and 9.95% respectively for the third straight week. However, the 91-day tenor maturity saw its yield edge up marginally by 02 basis points to 9.32%. The Public Debt Management Office (PDMO) raised only Rs. 80.611 billion or 80.61% in total out of the Rs. 100.00 billion offered in total. The 91-day tenor recorded acceptance above its respective target allocation, while the 182-day and 364-day recorded acceptances below their respective offered amounts. Total bids received amounted to 1.86 times the overall offer. A further amount of Rs. 2.28 billion was raised at the Phase 2 of the auction. In addition, the details of the Treasury Bond auction due to be held on Thursday, the 29th of October are as follows. The round of auctions will have a total offered amount of Rs. 100.00 billion across three available maturities. The auction will be comprised of: Rs. 40 billion from a 15 May 2030 maturity bearing a coupon rate of 11.00%; Rs. 40 billion from a 15 October 2034 maturity bearing a coupon rate of 11.70%; Rs. 20 billion from a 15 August 2036 maturity bearing a coupon rate of 10.85%; The settlement for which will be held on 2 November 2026. In the money market, the net liquidity surplus stood at Rs. 120.50 billion yesterday. A total of Rs. 93.75 billion was deposited at the Central Bank’s SDFR (Standing Deposit Facility Rate) of 8.25% while no funds were withdrawn from the Central Bank’s SLFR (Standing Lending Facility Rate) of 9.25%. In addition, the Domestic Operations Department (DOD) of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka mopped out Rs. 26.75 billion by way of an overnight repo auction at a weighted average yield of 8.75%. The weighted average yields on overnight call money and repos were recorded at 9.02% and 9.07% respectively. Forex market The USD/LKR rate on spot contracts was seen closing at Rs. 332.45/332.50 yesterday, with the rupee depreciating against its previous day’s closing of Rs. 332.25/332.40. The total USD/LKR traded volume for 26th October amounted to $ 53.75 million. (References: Public Debt Management Office - Ministry of Finance, Central Bank of Sri Lanka, Bloomberg E-Bond Trading Platform, Money Broking Companies)

audit.headline: Standard Capital mandatory offer awaits SEC nod
audit.summary: The mandatory offer by Abishek Sithampalam for the remaining 29.46% of Standard Capital PLC is awaiting a determination from the Securities and Exchange Commission of Sri Lanka (SEC), the company said yesterday. Sithampalam purchased 3,908,715 ordinary voting shares, or 70.54% of the company’s issued ordinary voting shares, on 2 October, 2026. The acquisition requires him to offer to buy the remaining 1,632,113 shares from minority shareholders. The company reported net assets of Rs. 26.59 per share as of end-June 2026 with Gulf East Finance Ltd., (31.76%), Standard Industries Ltd., (18.05%) and Amina Investments Ltd., (15.44%) and Eastern Ocean Investments Ltd., (9.14%) the top shareholders. The share ended yesterday up Rs. 2.80 at Rs. 44.60. On 2 October Sithampalam acquired 70.54% of voting shares at Rs. 40 each for over Rs. 156.3 million.
audit.body: The mandatory offer by Abishek Sithampalam for the remaining 29.46% of Standard Capital PLC is awaiting a determination from the Securities and Exchange Commission of Sri Lanka (SEC), the company said yesterday. audit.headline: The CIO Confluence 2026 brings together banking and tech leaders to shape intelligent banking era
audit.summary: Over 500 banking, technology and business leaders gathered at The CIO Confluence 2026 to explore how artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and intelligent customer engagement are reshaping the future of financial services. Held under the theme “Beyond Digital: The Intelligent Banking Era,” the event brought together senior industry stakeholders at Cinnamon Life City of Dreams, Colombo, for a day of keynote insights, technology perspectives, breakout sessions and panel discussions focused on the next phase of banking transformation. The event was graced by Central Bank of Sri Lanka Governor Dr. P. Nandalal Weerasinghe as Chief Guest, who described the theme as particularly timely given the pace at which technology is reshaping the financial sector.
audit.body: Over 500 banking, technology and business leaders gathered at The CIO Confluence 2026 to explore how artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and intelligent customer engagement are reshaping the future of financial services. Held under the theme “Beyond Digital: The Intelligent Banking Era,” the event brought together senior industry stakeholders at Cinnamon Life City of Dreams, Colombo, for a day of keynote insights, technology perspectives, breakout sessions and panel discussions focused on the next phase of banking transformation. The event was graced by Central Bank of Sri Lanka Governor Dr. P. Nandalal Weerasinghe as Chief Guest, who described the theme as particularly timely given the pace at which technology is reshaping the financial sector. “CIOs are no longer the custodians of IT infrastructure, but co-architects of economic trust, as you harness intelligence to drive hyper-personalisation and rapid innovation” said Dr. Weerasinghe. The Governor’s observation captured a central message of the Confluence: technology leadership in banking is increasingly extending beyond infrastructure and systems towards trust, innovation, customer experience and broader economic value. The program opened with a keynote by at 3A Ventures Partner-Asia and ASEAN Economic Forum, BIU Board of Advisers Cyrus Daruwala, who examined the evolving technology priorities of financial institutions and the shift towards more intelligent and outcome-driven banking models. This was followed by perspectives from the event’s technology partners, offering insights across AI, cybersecurity, enterprise infrastructure and digital transformation. The conference then moved into two focused sessions; “Cyber Security in the Age of AI” and “AI-Powered Customer Engagement”, addressing two critical dimensions of the intelligent banking journey. While the first explored the changing threat landscape and the need for adaptive security, the latter examined how AI can help financial institutions move from conventional personalisation towards more predictive and intelligent customer experiences. Two panel discussions further deepened the conversation. “AI vs. AI: Building a Zero-Trust Banking Ecosystem for the Next Generation of Cyber Threats” examined the evolving contest between AI-enabled attacks and AI-powered defence, while “From Personalization to Prediction: Reinventing Customer Engagement through Intelligent Banking” explored how data and intelligence are changing the way banks understand and serve their customers. The Confluence was supported by a strong ecosystem of technology partners, with South Asian Technologies Group as Platinum Sponsor and Huawei as Gold Sponsor. Pinnacle Sponsors included Pinnacle Distribution with Dell Technologies and VMware, and Redington with Red Hat. Silver Sponsors were Eguardian with Fortinet, Cryptogen with Palo Alto Networks, and Aurionpro. Dialog Enterprise was the Official Digital Connectivity Partner, while Daily FT was the Official Print Media Partner. With strong audience engagement throughout the program, The CIO Confluence 2026 provided a platform for banking and technology leaders to move beyond conversations around digital adoption and focus on the strategic role of intelligence, trust and innovation in shaping the next generation of financial services. The event reinforced a defining shift in the banking technology landscape: the question is no longer simply how institutions become digital, but how they become intelligent, secure and customer-centric by design.

audit.headline: 300,000-cylinder LPG shortage
audit.summary: 28 Oct 2026 | BY Buddhika Samaraweera Shortfall caused by shipment and unloading delays Litro releases 100,000 cylinders daily to replenish supplies CAA to be asked to probe reports of cylinders disappearing from market The shortage of about 250,000-300,000 domestic liquified petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders caused by the three and a half-day delay in the arrival and unloading of a gas shipment is expected to be resolved within seven to eight days, Deputy Trade Minister R M Jayawardena said, adding that the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) would be asked to investigate reports of cylinders disappearing from the market soon after being released. Speaking to The Daily Morning yesterday (27), he said that an LPG shipment had arrived around two days later than expected, followed by a further delay of about one and a half days in unloading the gas and transporting it for distribution.
audit.body: 28 Oct 2026 | BY Buddhika Samaraweera Shortfall caused by shipment and unloading delays Litro releases 100,000 cylinders daily to replenish supplies CAA to be asked to probe reports of cylinders disappearing from market The shortage of about 250,000-300,000 domestic liquified petroleum gas (LPG) cylinders caused by the three and a half-day delay in the arrival and unloading of a gas shipment is expected to be resolved within seven to eight days, Deputy Trade Minister R M Jayawardena said, adding that the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) would be asked to investigate reports of cylinders disappearing from the market soon after being released. Speaking to The Daily Morning yesterday (27), he said that an LPG shipment had arrived around two days later than expected, followed by a further delay of about one and a half days in unloading the gas and transporting it for distribution. "We usually release around 80,000 cylinders of 12.5 kg to the market daily. In that context, these delays created an estimated shortfall of between 250,000 and 300,000 12.5 kg cylinders in the market." To make up for this shortage, he said the Litro Gas Lanka Limited had been releasing 100,000 cylinders of 12.5 kg each to the market daily, continuously since the morning of 23 October. "The shortage should be eliminated within around seven or eight days. However, I have received reports that cylinders supplied to the market are selling out almost immediately. There is no way that they should be selling out immediately like that,” he said. Jayawardena further said that cylinders used by businesses could be exhausted within two or three days, but that those supplied for household use generally lasted around two and a half to three months. “Household cylinders cannot be running out that quickly. If they are disappearing from the market immediately after being released, that is a problem. We are planning to inform the CAA to carry out raids across the country and check whether cylinders are being hidden. If necessary, we will ask them to coordinate with District and Divisional Secretaries." Consumers in several areas have been facing difficulties in obtaining domestic gas cylinders in the past few days, with queues reported at some distribution points as households struggle to secure supplies.

audit.headline: 5-6 July Prison incident: Rs 3-5m compensation for each officer
audit.summary: Prisons Ordinance to be amended to empower Prison Tactical Force The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a set of recommendations to provide compensation and other assistance to prison officers who were killed or injured while on duty during clashes at a prison on 5 and 6 July. At its meeting held on 3 August, the Cabinet decided to appoint a committee headed by the Justice Ministry Secretary to make recommendations on compensation and assistance for the affected officers. The committee has since submitted its report, which was presented to the Cabinet by the Justice Minister. The Cabinet has approved the implementation of the recommendations outlined in the report.
audit.body: Prisons Ordinance to be amended to empower Prison Tactical Force The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a set of recommendations to provide compensation and other assistance to prison officers who were killed or injured while on duty during clashes at a prison on 5 and 6 July. At its meeting held on 3 August, the Cabinet decided to appoint a committee headed by the Justice Ministry Secretary to make recommendations on compensation and assistance for the affected officers. The committee has since submitted its report, which was presented to the Cabinet by the Justice Minister. The Cabinet has approved the implementation of the recommendations outlined in the report. In addition to compensation payable under the Public Administration Circular Number 22/936, the Cabinet has approved the following special payments: for officers killed in the line of duty Rs 5 million per officer, for officers who become fully disabled Rs 5 million per officer, for officers with partial disabilities resulting in a 100 per cent loss of the earning capacity Rs 4 million per officer, and for officers who sustained temporary partial disabilities Rs 3 million per officer. The Cabinet has also approved several measures to strengthen the Prison Tactical Force, including: amending the Prisons Ordinance to introduce provisions granting the Force legal status, recruiting a sufficient number of qualified personnel to strengthen the Force, providing specialised training in the relevant fields and equipping the Force with the necessary equipment, and taking steps to establish a headquarters for the Force. The measures are intended to provide support to affected prison officers while strengthening the operational capacity and preparedness of the Force.

audit.headline: AMLL: Financial system strength relies on institutions, regulations: PM
audit.summary: The strength of a country’s financial system depends not only on the laws and institutions established but also on their effectiveness, accountability, and integrity in practice, Prime Minister Dr Harini Amarasuriya said, as quoted in a statement made by the Prime Minister’s office recently (26). According to the statement, Dr Amarasuriya made the comments while participating in the inaugural meeting of Sri Lanka’s Third Mutual Evaluation on Anti-Money Laundering, Countering the Financing of Terrorism and Countering Proliferation Financing (AML/CFT/CPF), conducted by the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering (APG). Accordingly, she noted that Sri Lanka’s Third Mutual Evaluation provides an important opportunity to demonstrate the country’s progress in combating financial crime, identify areas requiring further improvement and strengthen alignment with international standards.

The Prime Minister reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to working constructively with the assessment team and all relevant stakeholders to strengthen Sri Lanka’s AML/CFT/CPF framework, address emerging risks and uphold the confidence of international partners and investors, the statement added.

audit.headline: Anti-Speaker NCM on 3 Nov
audit.summary: 28 Oct 2026 | BY Buddhika Samaraweera Parliament is scheduled to debate the Opposition’s revised No-Confidence Motion on 3 November. The Parliamentary agenda for the week was decided at a meeting of the Committee on Parliamentary Business, held under the Chairpersonship of Speaker Dr Jagath Wickramaratne. The Opposition is set to present its motion before Parliament. Meanwhile, the Parliamentary Secretariat is understood to share the Opposition’s position that the no-confidence motion (NCM) against the Speaker of Parliament Dr Jagath Wickramaratne was submitted in accordance with the proper procedures and established Parliamentary practices, despite the Ruling Party previously directing Parliamentary officials to remove the motion from the Order Book.
audit.body: 28 Oct 2026 | BY Buddhika Samaraweera Parliament is scheduled to debate the Opposition’s revised No-Confidence Motion on 3 November. The Parliamentary agenda for the week was decided at a meeting of the Committee on Parliamentary Business, held under the Chairpersonship of Speaker Dr Jagath Wickramaratne. The Opposition is set to present its motion before Parliament. Meanwhile, the Parliamentary Secretariat is understood to share the Opposition’s position that the no-confidence motion (NCM) against the Speaker of Parliament Dr Jagath Wickramaratne was submitted in accordance with the proper procedures and established Parliamentary practices, despite the Ruling Party previously directing Parliamentary officials to remove the motion from the Order Book. Sources within Parliament told The Daily Morning that the Government had earlier taken the position that the motion cannot be debated in its original form because it refers to matters currently before courts, invoking the sub judice rule. "However, the Opposition has refused to amend the text or submit a fresh motion, insisting that the original document must be taken up for debate. They maintained that the NCM was signed and submitted according to proper procedures and established practices. The Parliamentary Secretariat is of the same view." At a subsequent Parliament Business Committee meeting, both the Government and the Opposition had agreed to obtain the Attorney General’s (AG) advice on the matter. "However, the motion has yet to be referred to the AG." sources said yesterday. When contacted by The Daily Morning , AG, President's Counsel Parinda Ranasinghe Junior said that he was unaware of the developments surrounding the motion. The Opposition maintained that seeking the AG’s advice on an NCM against a Speaker is unprecedented in the Parliament’s history and that the process should not be used to delay a debate. Speaking to The Daily Morning on 19 October, Chief Opposition Whip Gayantha Karunathilleka said that the Government had not rejected the motion outright but had insisted on obtaining the AG’s advice before fixing a date for the debate. The NCM against Dr Wickramaratne was submitted to the Secretary-General of Parliament, attorney Kushani Rohanadheera on 9 October by 44 Opposition Parliamentarians representing the Samagi Jana Balawegaya, the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna, the New Democratic Front and independent groups. The motion alleges violations of the Constitution, the Anti-Corruption Act, the Offences Against Public Property Act, the Penal Code, the Right to Information Act, the Code of Conduct for MPs and the Standing Orders of Parliament.

audit.headline: Defence Ministry claims: Some Ditwah camp dwellers reluctant to leave
audit.summary: 28 Oct 2026 | BY Dhanushka Dharmapriya Some people displaced by Cyclone Ditwah are reluctant to leave relief camps where they continue to receive Government assistance, despite ongoing efforts to relocate them to safer housing, an official from the Defence Ministry said. Speaking to The Daily Morning , Additional Secretary (Disaster Management Division) at the Ministry, Dharmathilaka Gamage said that the Government continued to provide necessary facilities to camp residents while working to provide permanent housing solutions. However, the relocation process is progressing slowly due to a shortage of staff, he said. “Sometimes, people tend to complain that they are still in the camps and that the Government has not provided solutions yet, while continuing to receive the benefits,” Gamage said.
audit.body: 28 Oct 2026 | BY Dhanushka Dharmapriya Some people displaced by Cyclone Ditwah are reluctant to leave relief camps where they continue to receive Government assistance, despite ongoing efforts to relocate them to safer housing, an official from the Defence Ministry said. Speaking to The Daily Morning , Additional Secretary (Disaster Management Division) at the Ministry, Dharmathilaka Gamage said that the Government continued to provide necessary facilities to camp residents while working to provide permanent housing solutions. However, the relocation process is progressing slowly due to a shortage of staff, he said. “Sometimes, people tend to complain that they are still in the camps and that the Government has not provided solutions yet, while continuing to receive the benefits,” Gamage said. He said that regular reviews are being conducted and that the Government is continuing to provide the necessary facilities to those remaining in the camps. According to Gamage, only a small number of people remain in the camps because they cannot afford rent or find relatives with whom they can stay, while others are reluctant to leave. “The Government has only spent Rs 43 billion out of the Rs 150 billion allocated for housing construction yet. A further Rs 100 million is also to be allocated for next year (2027), while rental expenses are also being covered for those who need to rent accommodation”. Gamage said that Rs 22,948 million was being spent on constructing 8,574 houses that had been completely destroyed in Ditwah , while Rs 17,540 million was being spent on constructing 61,682 houses that had been partly damaged. For those unable to find land for relocation, interim houses would be constructed on their existing land until their permanent houses are built, he said. He added that 35 interim houses are currently being constructed in the Nuwara Eliya District. He also said that Rs 600,000 was allocated per person for those requiring interim housing assistance. Gamage concluded that the Government expected to spend at least Rs 100 billion out of the allocated budget by the end of 2026, with the aim of relocating more people to safer houses. His comments come amid concerns that another 3,162 families are displaced by adverse weather conditions intensified by Cyclone Arnab , while some people displaced by Ditwah in November 2025 continue to remain in relief camps to date.

audit.headline: Diplomatic and Executive neutrality: President’s message to Brazil’s Lula under fire
audit.summary: 28 Oct 2026 | BY Sulochana Ramiah Mohan Charitha Herath queries moral, political judgments on defeated camp Former Parliamentarian Prof Charitha Herath has questioned whether President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s message congratulating Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his Election victory appropriately reflects the diplomatic neutrality expected of a Head of State. While acknowledging the gesture, Herath said that President Dissanayake was entitled to his ideological preferences and political judgments as an individual and political leader. However, he said that statements made in the capacity of the President carry a broader institutional responsibility.
audit.body: 28 Oct 2026 | BY Sulochana Ramiah Mohan Charitha Herath queries moral, political judgments on defeated camp Former Parliamentarian Prof Charitha Herath has questioned whether President Anura Kumara Dissanayake’s message congratulating Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his Election victory appropriately reflects the diplomatic neutrality expected of a Head of State. While acknowledging the gesture, Herath said that President Dissanayake was entitled to his ideological preferences and political judgments as an individual and political leader. However, he said that statements made in the capacity of the President carry a broader institutional responsibility. On the President’s message, Herath said on social media that while congratulating da Silva was entirely appropriate, extending the message to include moral and political judgements about the defeated political camp raised questions about the diplomatic responsibilities of a national leader. President Dissanayake, in his message posted on social media, said that the Brazilian people had not merely won an Election but had defeated “the forces of corruption, division and political lies”. Describing da Silva’s victory as historic, the President said that it demonstrated that people could not be misled by “bankrupt political dynasties and the ghosts of the past who believe that might is greater than right”. He also congratulated da Silva on leading “the march of progress yet again”. Herath stressed that democracy required respect not only for electoral outcomes but also for the diversity of political choices made by citizens of other countries. Whether political families or dynasties should continue to exercise influence, he said, is ultimately a matter for the people of those countries to decide. To illustrate his point, Herath asked whether Indian Opposition Leader Rahul Gandhi’s family background should become a reason to question the democratic choice of Indian voters if they elected him Prime Minister. Further, he argued that there was an important distinction between expressing political solidarity and maintaining the diplomatic neutrality expected of a Head of State. “The Presidency represents the Nation as a whole, not merely a particular political tradition or ideological position,” Herath said, adding that respect for democratic pluralism and the political sovereignty of other Nations should remain essential considerations in Presidential communication.

audit.headline: HIP: LAUGFS Gas explores options for Laugfs Terminals
audit.summary: LAUGFS Gas PLC has officially informed shareholders and the Colombo Stock Exchange that it is engaging in preliminary, informal discussions regarding strategic options for its wholly owned subsidiary, LAUGFS Terminals Limited. LAUGFS Terminals Limited owns and operates a 30,000 MT liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) terminal situated at the Hambantota International Port. In a corporate disclosure submitted to Colombo Stock Exchange on Monday (26) the company confirmed it is holding exploratory talks with interested parties. The options currently under evaluation include commercial collaboration, securing outside investment, or the potential disposal of part or all of LAUGFS Gas PLC’s shareholding in the subsidiary. The company highlighted that no agreement has been reached concerning the structure or terms of any prospective transaction, and no definitive agreement has been executed.
